definition_zh: 流亡；流亡者；长期离乡；流放；使离开
definition_en: the state of being forced to live away from your own country, the person who lives this way, or the act of forcing someone out
core_image: 一个人背着行囊站在国境线外，回头望自己的家
scene: 诗人被迫离开故土，在异国住了十年才回来。The poet spent ten years in exile before returning home.
sceneCN: 这里 exile 是「流亡」（第 1 个义项：被迫离开本国、在外居住的状态）；句意：诗人流亡十年之后才回到家乡。

derivatives.zh: 由 exile 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「流亡时期的；与流亡有关的」
由动词 exile 加 -er 构成，义为「实施放逐的人」，较少使用

senses.title: Forced life abroad
senses.definition: the state of being forced to live away from your own country, usually for political reasons
senses.definitionCN: 被迫离开本国、在外国生活的状态，通常出于政治原因
senses.example: The writer lived in exile for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家流亡在外二十年。
senses.why: The Latin noun names the condition of one who has been sent out of the land, so the state comes before the person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词先指「被赶出土地」的处境，所以英语里「流亡状态」这一层意义先于「流亡者」这一层。

senses.title: A banished person
senses.definition: a person who is forced to live away from their own country
senses.definitionCN: 被迫离开本国、在外国生活的人
senses.example: The exiles gathered every Sunday to speak their own language.
senses.exampleCN: 流亡者们每周日聚在一起说自己的母语。
senses.why: Latin exsul means the banished person himself, so the same word names both the condition and the one who endures it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 exsul 本指「被放逐的那个人」，于是同一个词既能指处境，也能指承受处境的人。

senses.title: A long stay away from home
senses.definition: a long period spent away from your home or country, sometimes by your own choice
senses.definitionCN: 离开家乡或本国在外度过的一段长时间，有时出于自愿
senses.example: After the scandal she went into voluntary exile in the countryside.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻之后，她自愿到乡间过起离群索居的日子。
senses.why: Once the word means a stay outside the homeland, the reason for leaving can soften from compulsion to choice.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词只表示「离家在外的一段时间」之后，离开的原因就可以从被迫软化为自愿。

senses.title: To banish someone
senses.definition: to force someone to leave their country, especially as a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 强迫某人离开本国，尤指作为惩罚
senses.example: The government exiled the journalist after the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判之后，政府把那名记者流放出境。
senses.why: The verb turns the state into an act: someone is put outside the border by another person in power.
senses.whyCN: 动词把状态变成行为：有权者把某人放到国境之外。

senses.title: To drive out of a place or group
senses.definition: to force someone or something out of a place, group, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 迫使某人或某物离开某个地方、群体或活动
senses.example: Cheap imports have exiled many small workshops from the market.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价进口货把许多小作坊挤出了市场。
senses.why: If the border can be a country, it can also be a market or a circle, so exile widens into any forced exclusion.
senses.whyCN: 既然边界可以是国境，也可以是市场或圈子，exile 就扩展到任何「被赶出去」的处境。

intro.en: Exile comes through Old French from Latin exsilium, banishment, built on exsul, a banished person.
intro.cn: exile 经古法语来自拉丁语 exsilium（放逐），其词基 exsul 指「被放逐的人」。

items.en: Exsul names the person who has been sent out of the community.
items.cn: exsul 指被赶出共同体的那个人。

items.en: Exsilium is the noun for the state and the act of banishment.
items.cn: exsilium 是表示流放状态与流放行为的名词。

items.en: The second element is disputed: one reading takes solum, soil, another salire, to leap.
items.cn: 第二个词素的来源存疑：一说为 solum（土地），一说为 salire（跳）。

items.en: Exil carries the word into French with the same political sense.
items.cn: exil 把这个词带入法语，政治含义不变。

items.en: English adopts exile as both noun and verb in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪把 exile 同时用作名词与动词。

items.en: Modern usage extends it to any forced or chosen life away from home.
items.cn: 现代用法把它扩展到任何被迫或自愿的离乡生活。

note.en: Exile sits among words for banishment and among words for the people who endure it.
note.cn: exile 处在「放逐」与「被放逐者」两组词之间。

normalIntro.en: Exile is built on the Latin prefix for out, and its family and phrases repeat that one movement.
normalIntro.cn: exile 建立在拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀上，它的词族与搭配都在重复这一个动作。

normal.en: Exile begins with ex-, the Latin prefix for out.
normal.cn: exile 以拉丁语前缀 ex-（向外）开头。

normal.en: The same ex- appears in exit and expel, both about going or being sent out.
normal.cn: 同样的 ex- 也出现在 exit 与 expel 里，两者都与「出去」有关。

normal.en: Go into exile and live in exile are the two everyday frames.
normal.cn: 「go into exile」与「live in exile」是最常用的两个框架。

normal.en: A government exiles a person, and that person then lives as an exile.
normal.cn: 政府 exile 一个人，这个人此后就以 exile 的身份生活。

normal.en: Self-imposed exile shows that the word no longer requires force.
normal.cn: self-imposed exile 说明这个词已经不必包含强迫。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase at a border crossing, the homeland left behind you.
abstract.cn: 想象边境线上的一只手提箱，故土被留在身后。

abstract.en: Picture a face you know from the news, now speaking from another country.
abstract.cn: 想象一张你在新闻里见过的脸，如今在异国发声。

abstract.en: Picture a writer who chose a quiet village far from home.
abstract.cn: 想象一位作家，自己挑了一个离家很远的安静村子。

examples.en: The former minister has lived in exile since the coup.
examples.cn: 政变以来，这位前部长一直流亡在外。

examples.en: The court exiled him for life for treason.
examples.cn: 法庭以叛国罪判他终身流放。

examples.en: Many exiles still hope to return one day.
examples.cn: 许多流亡者仍希望有朝一日能够回去。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ exsul（被放逐的人）→ exsilium（放逐）→ 古法语 exil → 英语 exile；第二个词素一说为 solum（土地），一说为 salire（跳），词源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Exile starts as the state of being sent out of the homeland, then names the person, widens to any long stay away, and finally becomes the act of driving someone out.
sensesIntro.cn: exile 先指被赶出故土的状态，再指承受这种状态的人，随后扩展到任何长期离乡，最后落在「把某人赶出去」的动作上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a suitcase at the border, the homeland behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：边境线旁的一只手提箱，故土在身后。

branches.en: The state of being sent out of the country is the base sense.
branches.cn: 被赶出本国后的状态是最基础的义项。

branches.en: The person who lives in that state takes the same noun.
branches.cn: 活在这种状态里的人，用同一个名词来指称。

branches.en: A stay abroad can become a choice rather than a punishment.
branches.cn: 在外的一段日子可以从惩罚变成自愿的选择。

branches.en: The verb turns the state into an act performed by someone in power.
branches.cn: 动词把状态变成有权者实施的行为。

branches.en: Any border, from a country to a market, can produce exile.
branches.cn: 任何边界，从国境到市场，都能制造出被赶出去的处境。

intro.en: Exile is built from the Latin prefix ex- and the root behind exsul, with English exilic and exiler added later.
intro.cn: exile 由拉丁语前缀 ex- 与 exsul 的词根构成，英语后来再加上 exilic 与 exiler。

latinIntro.en: Latin exsul is the banished person and exsilium the banishment; the second element is still debated.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exsul 是被放逐者，exsilium 是放逐；第二个词素至今仍有争议。

items.example: The prefix marks the direction of the journey.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记了行程的方向。

items.example: Exsul supplies the person at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: exsul 提供了这个词的中心人物。

items.example: Exsilium names the state that follows.
items.exampleCN: exsilium 指随之而来的处境。

items.example: On this reading, the exile is the one out of his soil.
items.exampleCN: 按这种解释，被放逐者就是「离开自己土地的人」。

items.example: On the other reading, the exile has leapt out of the boundary.
items.exampleCN: 按另一种解释，被放逐者是「跳出边界的人」。

items.example: Exile keeps both the state and the person.
items.exampleCN: exile 同时保留了状态与人这两层。

items.example: The verb adds the hand that pushes.
items.exampleCN: 动词补上了「推出去的那只手」。

items.example: The suffix forms exilic.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 exilic。

items.example: Exilic describes the years in Babylon.
items.exampleCN: exilic 描述在巴比伦的那些年。

items.example: Exiler is rare and mostly literary.
items.exampleCN: exiler 很少见，多用于文学。

definition_en: to be real or present; to live, especially in difficult conditions; to survive on something
core_image: 一样东西真实地立在那里并持续下去
scene: 问题在于这种鸟是否真的还存在。The question is whether this bird still exists at all.
sceneCN: 这里 exist 是「存在」（第 1 个义项）；句意：问题在于这种鸟是否真的还存在。

derivatives.zh: 存在主义的；关于存在的

senses.title: Be real
senses.definition: to be real or present in the world
senses.definitionCN: 真实地存在于世界上
senses.example: Doubt still exists about the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 人们对这个计划仍有疑虑。
senses.why: The core sense is simply being there.
senses.whyCN: 核心义就是真实地「在那里」。

senses.title: Stay alive
senses.definition: to live, especially in hard conditions
senses.definitionCN: 生存，尤指在艰苦环境中活着
senses.example: These animals exist in the deepest caves.
senses.exampleCN: 这些动物生存在最深的洞穴里。
senses.why: Being present is narrowed to being alive.
senses.whyCN: 「存在」收窄为「活着」。

senses.title: Live on
senses.definition: to manage to live with very little of something
senses.definitionCN: 靠很少的东西勉强维持生活
senses.example: The family existed on rice and beans for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人靠米饭和豆子熬过了一个月。
senses.why: Survival is tied to a small source of support.
senses.whyCN: 生存被具体化为依赖微薄的来源。

intro.en: Exist comes from Latin exsistere, to come forth or appear.
intro.cn: exist 源自拉丁语 exsistere，意为「出现、显现」。

items.en: Exsistere joins ex- (out) with sistere (to stand).
items.cn: exsistere 由 ex-（向外）与 sistere（站立）构成。

items.en: Exsistere means to step out and appear.
items.cn: exsistere 意为迈出并显现。

items.en: Exister carries the sense of being present.

items.en: Existen names the state of being.

items.en: Exist covers both being real and staying alive.

items.en: Exist on adds the sense of surviving with little.

note.en: Exist means to be real; exit is a way out.

normal.en: Some fish exist in total darkness.

examples.en: They existed for years on a tiny income.

items.example: Sistere gives the idea of standing.

definition_en: a way out of a place; the act of leaving; to go out or leave
core_image: 一扇通向外面、可以走出去的门
scene: 观众从大厅后方的出口有序离场。The audience left through the exit at the back of the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 exit 是「出口」（第 1 个义项）；句意：观众从大厅后方的出口有序离场。

senses.title: Way out
senses.definition: a door or passage that leads out of a place
senses.definitionCN: 通向建筑物外面的门或通道
senses.example: The emergency exit is on your left.
senses.exampleCN: 紧急出口在您的左边。
senses.why: The core object is the opening that lets you out.
senses.whyCN: 核心形象是让人走出去的开口。

senses.title: Act of leaving
senses.definition: the act of leaving a place or situation
senses.definitionCN: 离开某地或某种处境的行为
senses.example: Her exit from the meeting was sudden.
senses.exampleCN: 她突然退出了会议。
senses.why: The opening is now the action of going through it.
senses.whyCN: 出口变成了穿过出口的动作。

senses.title: To leave
senses.definition: to go out of a place or leave a program
senses.definitionCN: 走出某地，或退出某个程序
senses.example: The actors exit from the right side of the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 演员从舞台右侧退场。
senses.why: The noun turns into the verb for going out.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示「走出去」的动词。

intro.en: Exit comes from Latin exitus, a going out, from exire.
intro.cn: exit 源自拉丁语 exitus（出去），来自 exire。

items.en: Exitus is the noun for a going out.
items.cn: exitus 是表示「出去」的名词。

items.en: Exire joins ex- (out) with ire (to go).
items.cn: exire 由 ex-（向外）与 ire（走）构成。

items.en: Exitus appears in stage directions.
items.cn: exitus 出现于舞台提示中。

items.en: Issue and exit share the same Latin source.
items.cn: issue 与 exit 同出一源。

items.en: Exit enters English as a stage direction.
items.cn: exit 最初作为舞台提示进入英语。

items.en: Exit now means any way out of a place.
items.cn: 如今 exit 泛指任何出口。

note.en: Exit is a way out; exist means to be real.
note.cn: exit 是出口，exist 则表示存在。

entries.definition: to be real or present
to make someone eager or lively
to use effort or power
an opening into a room or building
a way out or a place to release something
the act of leaving a place

normalIntro.en: Exit is the door out and the act of leaving.
normalIntro.cn: exit 既是出去的门，也是离开的动作。

normal.en: The exit sign glowed above the door.
normal.cn: 出口标志在门上方发着光。

normal.en: They made a quick exit when the rain started.
normal.cn: 雨一开始下，他们就迅速离开了。

normal.en: Please exit through the rear door.
normal.cn: 请从后门离开。

normal.en: The stage direction told him to exit left.
normal.cn: 舞台提示让他从左侧退场。

normal.en: The emergency exit was blocked by boxes.
normal.cn: 紧急出口被箱子挡住了。

abstract.en: Picture an open door with light beyond it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇敞开的门，门后有光。

abstract.en: Imagine stepping out of a crowded room.
abstract.cn: 想象从拥挤的房间里走出去。

abstract.en: Think of a green sign pointing away.
abstract.cn: 想象一块指向远方的绿色指示牌。

examples.en: The nearest exit is beside the stairs.
examples.cn: 最近的出口在楼梯旁边。

examples.en: The singer made a dramatic exit from the stage.
examples.cn: 那位歌手戏剧性地退场了。

examples.en: Passengers exited the train in a hurry.
examples.cn: 乘客们匆匆忙忙地下了火车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exit」可拆成 ex（出）+ it（走）：走出去的地方就是「出口」。

root: 拉丁语 exitus（出去）来自 exire（走出），其中 ex- 表示「向外」，ire 表示「走」。

sensesIntro.en: Exit means a way out, the act of leaving, or to leave a place.
sensesIntro.cn: exit 意为出口、离场的行为，或离开某地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door that leads outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇通向外面的门。

branches.en: The physical opening is the core sense.
branches.cn: 实体的出口是核心义。

branches.en: Going through it becomes the act of leaving.
branches.cn: 穿过出口成为离开的行为。

branches.en: The act becomes a verb for leaving.
branches.cn: 这一行为转为表示离开的动词。

branches.en: The door and the departure belong together.
branches.cn: 门与离去相互关联。

branches.en: Noun and verb describe the same movement.
branches.cn: 名词与动词描述同一个动作。

intro.en: Exit joins Latin ex- (out) with ire (to go).
intro.cn: exit 由拉丁语 ex-（向外）与 ire（走）组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin exire and its noun exitus are the direct sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exire 及其名词 exitus 是直接来源。

items.exampleCN: ex- 表示向外走。

items.example: Ire supplies the movement in exit.
items.exampleCN: ire 为 exit 提供「走」的含义。

items.example: Exire is the verb behind exit.
items.exampleCN: exire 是 exit 背后的动词。

items.example: Exitus gives the noun its shape.
items.exampleCN: exitus 为这个名词提供词形。

items.example: Exit names the opening.
items.exampleCN: exit 指这个出口。

items.example: -S marks exits as plural.
items.exampleCN: -s 使 exits 成为复数。

items.example: -Ed forms the past exited.
items.exampleCN: -ed 构成过去式 exited。

items.example: Exiting appears in safety notices.
items.exampleCN: exiting 常见于安全提示中。

latinEntries.example: Ire is a basic verb of motion.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ire 是表示移动的基本动词。

definition_zh: （大批人的）离去；迁徙潮；外流；《出埃及记》
definition_en: a situation in which a large number of people leave a place at the same time, or the biblical book that tells of the Israelites leaving Egypt
core_image: 拂晓时分，望不到尾的队伍推着行李走出城门
scene: 工厂关门以后，年轻家庭开始陆续搬离这座小镇。After the factory closed, a slow exodus of young families began.
sceneCN: 这里 exodus 是「大批离去」（第 1 个义项：许多人同时离开一个地方）；句意：工厂关门以后，年轻家庭开始陆续搬走。

pos.zh: 大批离去；迁徙潮；外流；《出埃及记》

derivatives.zh: 与 exodus 同出希腊语 exodos 的旧式同源名词，义为「离去」，也曾用来指《出埃及记》，今已罕用
同源于希腊语 hodos（路）的名词，义为「一段插曲；一集」，并非由 exodus 直接派生
同源于希腊语 hodos（路）的名词，义为「时期；周期」，原义是「绕行一圈的路」

senses.title: A mass departure
senses.definition: a situation in which a large number of people leave a place at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 许多人同时离开一个地方的情形
senses.example: The announcement set off an exodus of foreign staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这项声明引发了外籍员工的大批离去。
senses.why: Greek exodos literally means a going out, so the word keeps the picture of many feet crossing one boundary.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 exodos 字面就是「走出去」，因此这个词保留了众人同时跨过同一条边界的画面。

senses.title: A flow of money or talent
senses.definition: a large-scale departure of money, jobs, or skilled people from a place
senses.definitionCN: 资金、工作岗位或技术人才大规模离开某地
senses.example: High rents have driven a steady exodus of artists from the district.
senses.exampleCN: 高昂的房租使艺术家持续迁出这个街区。
senses.why: Once the word means a crowd leaving, that crowd can be made of capital or skills instead of people.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「一大群东西离开」，这群东西就可以是资本或技能，而不必是人。

senses.title: The biblical book
senses.definition: the second book of the Bible, which tells how the Israelites left Egypt
senses.definitionCN: 《圣经》第二卷，讲述以色列人离开埃及的经过
senses.example: The story of the burning bush appears in Exodus.
senses.exampleCN: 燃烧的荆棘的故事见于《出埃及记》。
senses.why: The Greek title of that book was Exodus, so the name of one journey became the title of the book that records it.
senses.whyCN: 那卷书的希腊语标题就是 Exodus，一次行程的名字于是成了记载这次行程的书名。

senses.title: A walkout from an organization
senses.definition: a sudden departure of many members from a group, party, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 许多成员突然离开某个团体、政党或组织
senses.example: The scandal prompted an exodus of senior ministers.
senses.exampleCN: 这起丑闻促使多位高级部长集体去职。
senses.why: A party or a cabinet has borders of its own, so the crowd leaving a country can become a crowd leaving a room.
senses.whyCN: 政党和内阁也有自己的边界，于是「离开国家的一群人」可以变成「离开一间屋子的一群人」。

intro.en: Exodus comes from Greek exodos, a going out, which Latin and then English first used as the title of a book and later as a word for any mass departure.
intro.cn: exodus 来自希腊语 exodos（走出去），拉丁语与英语先把它用作书名，后来才泛指任何大批离去。

items.en: Exodos is built from ex, out, and hodos, way or road.
items.cn: exodos 由 ex（向外）与 hodos（路）构成。

items.en: In the Greek Bible the title names the Israelites going out of Egypt.
items.cn: 在希腊语圣经中，这个标题指以色列人走出埃及。

items.en: Exodus keeps the title and passes it to the church languages.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 exodus 保留了这个书名，并把它传给教会语言。

items.en: English uses Exodus for the second book of the Bible from its earliest period.
items.cn: 英语从最早时期就用 Exodus 指《圣经》第二卷。

items.en: Writers begin to use exodus for any large departure of people.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，作家开始用 exodus 泛指任何大批人的离开。

items.en: Modern usage extends the crowd to money, jobs, and talent.
items.cn: 现代用法把这里的「人群」扩展到资金、岗位与人才。

note.en: One group holds the Greek family built on hodos, road; the other holds words for leaving in numbers.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊语 hodos（路）的词族；第二组是表示「大批离开」的说法。

entries.definition: one part of a story or series, from Greek epeisodion, an addition on the way
entries.definitionCN: 故事或系列中的一集；与 exodus 同出 hodos（路），原指「路上加进来的一段」

entries.definition: a way of doing something, from Greek methodos, a following after
entries.definitionCN: 方法；与 exodus 同出 hodos（路），原义是「沿着一条路追赶」

entries.definition: a length of time, from Greek periodos, a going around
entries.definitionCN: 时期；与 exodus 同出 hodos（路），原义是「绕行一圈」

entries.definition: movement of people or animals from one region to another
entries.definitionCN: 人口或动物从一个地区迁往另一个地区

entries.definition: the act of leaving a place, with or without a crowd
entries.definitionCN: 离开某地的行为，不论有没有人群

entries.definition: the act of running away from danger

normalIntro.en: Exodus is a Greek compound whose two halves still show: the outward prefix and the word for road.
normalIntro.cn: exodus 是一个希腊语复合词，两半至今可见：向外的前缀与「路」这个词。

normal.en: Exodus begins with ex-, the Greek and Latin prefix for out.
normal.cn: exodus 以希腊语与拉丁语前缀 ex-（向外）开头。

normal.en: The second half is hodos, Greek for road, so an exodus is literally a road out.
normal.cn: 后半部分是希腊语 hodos（路），所以 exodus 字面就是「一条出去的路」。

normal.en: Mass exodus and rural exodus are the two most common frames.
normal.cn: 「mass exodus」与「rural exodus」是最常见的两个框架。

normal.en: A capital letter marks the biblical book, a small letter marks any crowd leaving.
normal.cn: 首字母大写指《出埃及记》，小写则指任何一群人的离开。

normal.en: Exodus is stronger than departure because it always implies numbers.
normal.cn: exodus 比 departure 更强，因为它总是含有「人数众多」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a road at dawn carrying more people than it can hold.
abstract.cn: 想象拂晓的一条路，装的人比路能容纳的还多。

abstract.en: Picture an office emptied of its designers in a single month.
abstract.cn: 想象一间办公室，一个月内设计师全部走空。

abstract.en: Picture an open book whose page shows a crowd crossing the sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一本摊开的书，页面上是人群穿过大海。

examples.en: The war caused an exodus of nearly two million people.
examples.cn: 战争导致近两百万人出走。

examples.en: Many tech firms left the city in a quiet exodus.
examples.cn: 许多科技公司悄然迁出了这座城市。

examples.en: The book of Exodus gives the word its capital letter.
examples.cn: 《出埃及记》给了这个词大写的形式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挨个得走」——城里人挨个离开，最后只剩空街；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 ex（向外）+ hodos（路）→ exodos（走出去）→ 晚期拉丁语 exodus（《出埃及记》）→ 英语 exodus；核心义是「一条向外走的路」。

sensesIntro.en: Exodus starts as the going out of a whole people, becomes the title of the book that records one such journey, and then widens to any outflow of money, jobs, or members.
sensesIntro.cn: exodus 先指一整个民族的走出，随后成为记载那次行程的书名，再扩展到资金、岗位与成员的外流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road at dawn carrying more people than it can hold.
core.cn: 核心意象：拂晓的一条路，人多得装不下。

branches.en: THE CROWD: many people leave one place at the same time.
branches.cn: 人群：许多人同时离开同一个地方。

branches.en: THE FLOW: capital and skills leave in the same shape.
branches.cn: 流出：资本与技能以同样的形态离开。

branches.en: THE BOOK: one such going out became a title.
branches.cn: 书名：一次这样的走出成了一个标题。

branches.en: THE GROUP: members can leave a party or a cabinet in numbers.
branches.cn: 团体：成员可以成群地离开一个政党或内阁。

branches.en: A country and a cabinet both have borders to cross.
branches.cn: 国境与内阁都有可以跨过的边界。

intro.en: Exodus is a Greek compound of a prefix and a root, and English built almost nothing on top of it.
intro.cn: exodus 是希腊语「前缀加词根」的复合词，英语几乎没有在它上面再加构词成分。

latinIntro.en: Greek ex means out and hodos means way; Latin borrowed the whole word as a title.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 ex 意为「向外」，hodos 意为「路」；拉丁语把整词借来作书名。

items.example: The prefix points the journey outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把行程指向外面。

items.example: Hodos supplies the road inside exodus.
items.exampleCN: hodos 提供了 exodus 内部的那条路。

items.example: Exodos is the direct source of the word.
items.exampleCN: exodos 是这个词的直接来源。

items.meaning: a going out, the biblical title
items.example: Latin keeps the word as the name of a book.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个词保留为书名。

items.meaning: the second book of the Bible
items.example: The capital letter belongs to the book.
items.exampleCN: 大写形式属于这卷书。

items.example: The common noun names any crowd leaving.
items.exampleCN: 普通名词指任何一群人的离开。

items.example: Episode carries the same road root.
items.exampleCN: episode 带着同一个「路」词根。

items.example: Period is a going around on the same road.
items.exampleCN: period 是在同一条路上绕行一圈。

latinEntries.meaning: a going out, the biblical title

definition_en: much too expensive, or much greater than is fair or reasonable
core_image: 价签上的数字长得拖到货架外面，顾客把手缩了回去
scene: 节日期间，这家酒店为一间普通客房开出了高得离谱的价钱。During the festival, the hotel charged exorbitant prices for a plain room.
sceneCN: 这里 exorbitant 是「过高的」（第 1 个义项：价格或费用高得不合理）；句意：节日期间，这家酒店为一间普通客房开出了离谱的价钱。

derivatives.zh: 由 exorbitant 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「过高；离谱」
由 exorbitant 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「过高地；离谱地」
exorbitance 的异体形式，义为「过度；无节制」，今较少使用

senses.title: Far too expensive
senses.definition: priced far above what is fair or usual
senses.definitionCN: 价格远远高于公平或通常的水平
senses.example: Ten pounds for a sandwich is exorbitant.
senses.exampleCN: 一个三明治十英镑，实在太贵了。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to leave the track, and a price that leaves the track of fair value is exorbitant.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「偏离轨道」，价格一旦偏离公道的轨道，就成了 exorbitant。

senses.title: Excessive in amount
senses.definition: much greater in size or amount than is reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 在规模或数量上远远超过合理程度
senses.example: The union rejected the exorbitant demands of the owners.
senses.exampleCN: 工会拒绝了资方提出的过分要求。
senses.why: Once the image is a deviation, any quantity can overshoot its proper line, not only money.
senses.whyCN: 意象一旦是「偏离」，越界的就可以是任何数量，而不只是钱。

senses.title: Off its path in old astronomy
senses.definition: moving outside its proper path, a sense once used of planets
senses.definitionCN: 偏离应有路径的，旧时用于描述行星
senses.example: Early writers on the stars called a planet exorbitant when it left its expected path.
senses.exampleCN: 早期研究星辰的作家把偏离预期路径的行星称为 exorbitant。
senses.why: The word began as a description of heavenly bodies leaving their orbits, and only much later turned to prices.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初描述天体离开轨道，很久以后才转向价格。

intro.en: Exorbitant comes from Latin exorbitare, to leave the track, built on ex, out of, and orbita, a wheel rut or orbit.
intro.cn: exorbitant 来自拉丁语 exorbitare（离开车辙、脱离轨道），由 ex（离开）与 orbita（车辙、轨道）构成。

items.en: Orbita is the rut left by a wheel and, by extension, the path of a heavenly body.
items.cn: orbita 是车轮留下的辙痕，引申为天体的运行轨道。

items.en: Exorbitare means to leave that track, a verb used of planets and of anything straying.
items.cn: exorbitare 意为离开这条轨道，既用于行星，也用于任何走偏之物。

items.en: The participle exorbitans describes what has gone off its path.
items.cn: 分词 exorbitans 描述已经离开原路的事物。

items.en: English adopts exorbitant for anything deviating from the right course.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪用 exorbitant 指偏离正路的一切。

items.en: The sense narrows to prices and demands that overshoot what is fair.
items.cn: 词义收窄到越过公道的价格与要求。

items.en: Today the word is almost always about money, cost, or appetite.
items.cn: 今天这个词几乎只用于金钱、成本或欲望。

note.en: One group is the orbit family; the other is the scale of prices that are simply too high.
note.cn: 第一组是「轨道」词族；第二组是「价格过高」这一语义场。

entries.definition: the quality of being exorbitant
entries.definitionCN: 过高；离谱，由 exorbitant 加 -ance 构成的名词

entries.definition: in a way that is far too expensive
entries.definitionCN: 过高地；离谱地，由 exorbitant 加 -ly 构成的副词

entries.definition: the curved path of a body around another body
entries.definitionCN: 天体绕行的轨道；与 exorbitant 同出拉丁语 orbita（车辙），只是前缀不同

entries.definition: more than is necessary or reasonable
far too expensive, used especially of prices
entries.definitionCN: （价格）过高的；带有敲诈意味的

entries.definition: raised above a true or fair level

normalIntro.en: Exorbitant keeps the Latin wheel rut inside it: a price that has left the rut of fair value.
normalIntro.cn: exorbitant 内部保留着拉丁语「车辙」：价格一旦驶出公道的车辙，就是它。

normal.en: Exorbitant keeps the Latin orbita, a wheel rut, inside it.
normal.cn: exorbitant 内部保留着拉丁语 orbita（车辙）。

normal.en: The prefix ex- means out, so the word says the price has left its rut.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex- 意为「出」，所以这个词是在说价格驶出了车辙。

normal.en: It is almost always used of money: prices, fees, rent, costs.
normal.cn: 它几乎总用于钱：价格、费用、租金、成本。

normal.en: Exorbitant is stronger than expensive, because it adds unfairness.
normal.cn: exorbitant 比 expensive 更强，因为它多了一层「不公平」。

normal.en: The adverb exorbitantly and the noun exorbitance keep the same judgement.
normal.cn: 副词 exorbitantly 与名词 exorbitance 保留同样的评判。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag so long that it hangs off the shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签长得垂到货架外面。

abstract.en: Picture a demand letter so thick that it needs two envelopes.
abstract.cn: 想象一封要求信厚到要装两个信封。

abstract.en: Picture a planet slipping out of its orbit and cutting across another sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗行星滑出自己的轨道，横穿别人的天空。

examples.en: The city has some of the most exorbitant rents in the country.
examples.cn: 这座城市的租金在全国属于最离谱的一档。

examples.en: They were charged an exorbitant fee for changing the date.
examples.cn: 他们改签日期被收了一笔高得离谱的费用。

examples.en: Exorbitant spending brought the club close to ruin.
examples.cn: 毫无节制的开销让俱乐部濒临破产。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一个坐地摊」——摊主开价高得离谱；这只是拆读联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex（离开）+ orbita（车辙、轨道）→ exorbitare（脱离轨道）→ 晚期拉丁语分词 exorbitans → 英语 exorbitant；本义「偏离轨道」，今多指价格与要求高得离谱。

sensesIntro.en: Exorbitant begins as a description of bodies leaving their orbit, then of anything off the right course, and finally settles on prices and demands that overshoot fair limits.
sensesIntro.cn: exorbitant 先描述天体离开轨道，再指任何偏离正路的事物，最后落在越过公道限度的价格与要求上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a price tag hanging off the shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张垂到货架外的价签。

branches.en: PRICE: the everyday sense, money far above fair value.
branches.cn: 价格：最日常的义项，钱远远超过公道价值。

branches.en: AMOUNT: any quantity can overshoot its proper line.
branches.cn: 数量：任何数量都可能越过应有的界限。

branches.en: OLD SKY: the earliest sense, a planet off its path.
branches.cn: 旧日星空：最早的义项，偏离路径的行星。

branches.en: A bill and a claim are judged against the same fair line.
branches.cn: 一张账单与一项要求，对的是同一条公道线。

branches.en: The price sense still keeps the old image of leaving a track.
branches.cn: 价格义至今仍保留着「驶出车辙」的旧意象。

intro.en: Exorbitant is a Latin prefix and root with an English adjective ending, and the orbit family can be read from it.
intro.cn: exorbitant 由拉丁语前缀、词根与英语形容词词尾构成，从它可以直接读出「轨道」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex means out of, orbita means a wheel rut or orbit, and the participle ending -ant describes being in that state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ex 意为「离开」，orbita 意为「车辙、轨道」，分词词尾 -ant 表示正处于该状态。

items.example: The prefix marks the departure from the track.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记「离开车辙」的方向。

items.example: Orbita gives the image of a fixed path.
items.exampleCN: orbita 提供了一条固定路径的意象。

items.example: Exorbitare is the verb behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: exorbitare 是这个形容词背后的动词。

items.example: The participle passes into English as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词以形容词身份进入英语。

items.example: Exorbitant keeps only the judgement, not the road.
items.exampleCN: exorbitant 只留下评判，不再提那条路。

items.example: The suffix forms exorbitance.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 exorbitance。

items.meaning: the state of being too high
items.example: Exorbitance names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: exorbitance 直接命名这种性质。

items.example: The suffix forms exorbitantly.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 exorbitantly。

items.example: Exorbitantly prices a stay out of reach.
items.exampleCN: exorbitantly 把花费抬到够不着的地方。

items.meaning: the path of a body in space
items.example: Orbit is the same root without the prefix.
items.exampleCN: orbit 是去掉前缀的同一个词根。

definition_zh: 外骨骼；节肢动物体表起支撑与保护作用的硬壳；几丁质表皮本身；甲壳类与贝类的钙质外壳；蜕下的旧壳；化石中的外骨骼；可穿戴的机械外骨骼；建筑或器械的外部承力骨架（比喻）
definition_en: a hard outer covering that supports and protects the body of an arthropod or other invertebrate, lying outside the soft tissues
core_image: 潮间带的石头上，一只蟹抬起青灰色的硬壳，关节间露出薄薄的软膜
scene: 潮间带的石头上，一只蟹抬起硬壳，关节间露出薄薄的软膜。On the tidal rock, a crab lifts its hard exoskeleton on thin flexible joints.
sceneCN: 这里 exoskeleton 指「节肢动物体表起支撑与保护作用的硬壳」（第 1 个义项：外骨骼）；句意为潮间带石头上的一只蟹抬起硬壳，关节处只留薄膜相连。可辨识物件：青灰硬壳、关节薄膜、石面、蟹步足。

pos.zh: 外骨骼；甲壳；外部承力骨架

senses.title: A hard outer support
senses.titleCN: 起支撑与保护作用的外部硬壳
senses.definition: a rigid outer covering that gives the body shape and protection while the muscles attach inside it
senses.definitionCN: 坚硬的包被，为身体定形并提供保护，肌肉在其内侧附着
senses.example: On the tidal rock, a crab lifts its hard exoskeleton on thin flexible joints.
senses.exampleCN: 潮间带的石头上，一只蟹抬起硬壳，关节处只留薄膜相连。
senses.why: The word says where the support lies: outside the soft body, opposite to our own internal frame.
senses.whyCN: 这个词说明了支撑的位置：在柔软身体之外，与我们的内置支架相反。

senses.title: The chitinous cuticle
senses.definition: the layered cuticle of chitin and protein that forms the outer body wall of insects and crustaceans
senses.definitionCN: 由几丁质与蛋白质分层构成、成为昆虫与甲壳类体壁的外层
senses.example: The insect's exoskeleton is a cuticle that must be shed to allow growth.
senses.exampleCN: 昆虫的外骨骼是一层必须蜕去才能生长的表皮。
senses.why: This technical sense identifies the material, not just the function, and it explains why the animal must moult.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义指出材料而非仅指功能，也解释了动物为何必须蜕皮。

senses.title: A calcareous shell
senses.titleCN: 钙质外壳（甲壳类与贝类）
senses.definition: a shell hardened with calcium carbonate, as in crabs, barnacles or molluscs
senses.definitionCN: 以碳酸钙硬化的外壳，如蟹、藤壶或软体动物
senses.example: Barnacles build a calcareous exoskeleton around themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 藤壶在自己周围造出钙质外壳。
senses.why: Shells are one kind of exoskeleton, but not every shell is an arthropod cuticle, so the words overlap only partly.
senses.whyCN: 壳是外骨骼的一种，但并非所有壳都是节肢动物表皮，两词只是部分重叠。

senses.title: A cast-off outer casing
senses.definition: the old covering left behind after moulting, often found intact and empty
senses.definitionCN: 蜕皮后留下的旧包被，常完整而空心地被发现
senses.example: A dry exoskeleton clung to the reed at the pond edge.
senses.exampleCN: 一具干枯的旧壳粘在池边的芦苇上。
senses.why: This sense focuses on the object rather than the living animal, which matters when ecologists count moults.
senses.whyCN: 这一义聚焦物件而非活体，生态学家清点蜕壳时正需要这个意思。

senses.title: Fossil outer coverings
senses.definition: the preserved outer skeleton of extinct arthropods, often the only part that survives
senses.definitionCN: 已灭绝节肢动物被保存下来的外壳，常是唯一留存的部分
senses.example: Trilobite exoskeletons are common in Cambrian shale.
senses.exampleCN: 三叶虫的外骨骼在寒武纪页岩中很常见。
senses.why: Because the hard part is outside, fossil record is biased toward exoskeletons, a point palaeontology always notes.
senses.whyCN: 由于坚硬部分在体外，化石记录偏向保存外骨骼，古生物学总会强调这一点。

senses.title: A wearable mechanical frame
senses.definition: a powered frame worn outside the body to support or amplify movement
senses.definitionCN: 穿在身体外部、用于支撑或放大动作的动力框架
senses.example: The worker wore an exoskeleton that carried the load to his hips.
senses.exampleCN: 工人穿了一副把重量传到髋部的机械外骨骼。
senses.why: Engineering copied the biological word because the frame, like a shell, carries forces outside the soft body.
senses.whyCN: 工程学仿用了这个生物词，因为框架如外壳一样，在柔软身体之外承担力量。

senses.title: An external load-bearing frame
senses.titleCN: 建筑或器械的外部承力骨架
senses.definition: a structure that carries loads on its outside, as in some towers or vehicle chassis
senses.definitionCN: 在外侧承担荷载的结构，如某些塔架或车辆底盘
senses.example: The tower's exoskeleton of steel tubes takes the wind load.
senses.exampleCN: 这座塔的钢管外骨架承受风荷载。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from animals to structures but keeps the key idea: strength outside, softness inside.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从动物移到结构，却保留了要点：外强内柔。

senses.title: A protective outward manner
senses.definition: a hard outward manner or system that shields something softer inside
senses.definitionCN: 一层坚硬的对外姿态或制度，保护其中较柔软的部分
senses.example: His exoskeleton of rules hid a very anxious man.
senses.exampleCN: 他那层规章的外壳藏着一个极焦虑的人。
senses.why: The metaphor is emotional rather than mechanical: the shell protects but also isolates.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻是情感性的而非机械性的：外壳既保护也隔离。

intro.en: Exoskeleton joins Greek exo- 'outside' to skeleton, from Greek skeletos 'dried up, a mummy'. Nineteenth-century comparative anatomy coined the term to contrast with endoskeleton.
intro.cn: exoskeleton 把希腊 exo-「外面」与 skeleton 组合，后者出自希腊 skeletos「干枯的、木乃伊」。19 世纪比较解剖学造出这个词，与 endoskeleton 对照。

items.en: Exo- meant 'outside, outward' and remains productive in English, as in exoskeleton, exothermic and exoplanet.
items.cn: exo- 意为「外面、向外」，在英语中仍能产词，如 exoskeleton、exothermic、exoplanet。

items.en: Skeleton came from Greek skeletos 'dried up', used of a mummy or a withered body, and only later meant the bony frame.
items.cn: skeleton 出自希腊 skeletos「干枯的」，本用于木乃伊或干瘪的尸体，后来才指骨性支架。

items.en: Nineteenth-century anatomists needed paired terms for internal and external supports, and exoskeleton was formed against the older endoskeleton.
items.cn: 19 世纪解剖学家需要一对表示内外支撑的术语，exoskeleton 是对较早的 endoskeleton 造出的对应词。

items.en: The word was applied to insects, crustaceans and molluscs, and to the cuticle as well as the shell.
items.cn: 这个词被用于昆虫、甲壳类与软体动物，既指外壳也指表皮。

items.en: In the twentieth and twenty-first centuries the term was borrowed for wearable frames and external building structures.
items.cn: 在 20 与 21 世纪，这个词被借用于可穿戴框架与建筑外骨架。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and coiner): the exact first use and whether one anatomist coined both terms together are not settled, so no single attribution should be treated as certain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与首创者）：确切最早的用法、以及是否由同一位解剖学家造出这对术语，均无定论，不应把单一归属当作确定。

note.en: Group one sets exoskeleton against the internal frame and its own derivatives; group two lists the outer coverings that overlap with it.
note.cn: 第一组把 exoskeleton 与内骨骼及自身派生词对照；第二组列出与它语义重叠的外层包被。

entries.definition: An endoskeleton lies inside the soft tissue, as in vertebrates, so the two words name opposite arrangements.
entries.definitionCN: endoskeleton 位于软组织之内，如脊椎动物，两词指相反的布局。

entries.definition: Skeleton is the general word and can mean either arrangement, or a framework of any kind.
entries.definitionCN: skeleton 是通称，可指任一种布局，也可指任何骨架。

entries.definition: Exoskeletal describes what belongs to an outer skeleton and cannot replace the noun.
entries.definitionCN: exoskeletal 描述属外骨骼之物，不能替代名词。

entries.definition: The adverb is rare and mainly appears in technical description, not in general prose.
entries.definitionCN: 这个副词罕见，主要用于技术描述，不用于一般行文。

entries.definition: A shell is a hard outer covering, often calcareous; it may or may not be a true exoskeleton.
entries.definitionCN: shell 是坚硬外层，常为钙质；它可能是也可能不是真正的外骨骼。

entries.definition: A carapace is the shield covering the back of a crab or similar animal, part of its exoskeleton.
entries.definitionCN: carapace 指蟹类背部的甲盾，是外骨骼的一部分。

entries.definition: A cuticle is the outermost layer of an animal or plant; in arthropods it is the exoskeleton itself.
entries.definitionCN: cuticle 指动物或植物的最外层；在节肢动物身上它就是外骨骼。

entries.definition: Armour is the general word for protective covering, used of tanks and knights as well as animals.
entries.definitionCN: armour 是防护包被的通称，可用于坦克、骑士，也可用于动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Exo- 'outside' plus skeleton says exactly where the support sits.
normal.cn: exo-「外面」加 skeleton 直接说明支撑的位置。

normal.en: The family runs exoskeleton, exoskeletons, exoskeletal and exoskeletally.
normal.cn: 词族包括 exoskeleton、exoskeletons、exoskeletal 与 exoskeletally。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: shed the exoskeleton, robotic exoskeleton, calcareous exoskeleton.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：蜕去外骨骼、机械外骨骼、钙质外壳。

normal.en: The pair endoskeleton and exoskeleton differ only in the first prefix, endo- versus exo-.
normal.cn: 内骨骼与外骨骼这一对只差前缀：endo- 与 exo-。

normal.en: Arthropods must moult because their support cannot grow with them.
normal.cn: 节肢动物必须蜕皮，因为它们的支撑结构不能随身体一同长大。

abstract.en: Picture a knight whose armour is grown, not worn.
abstract.cn: 想象一位骑士，盔甲是长出来的，不是穿上的。

abstract.en: Picture a building that wears its steel frame on the outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一座把钢架穿在外面的建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose politeness is a shell with a soft animal inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人，礼貌是壳，里面藏着一只柔软的小动物。

examples.en: A crab must back out of its old exoskeleton before the new one hardens.
examples.cn: 蟹必须在新壳硬化之前从旧壳里退出来。

examples.en: Paleontologists rely on exoskeletons because soft parts rarely fossilise.
examples.cn: 古生物学家依赖外骨骼，因为软体部分极少形成化石。

examples.en: The warehouse adopted a robotic exoskeleton to help workers lift heavy crates.
examples.cn: 仓库采用机械外骨骼来帮助工人抬起重箱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exo（外）+ skeleton（骨架）」——长在身体外面的骨架 → 外骨骼

root: 希腊 exo-「外面」+ skeleton（希腊 skeletos「干枯的」，原指木乃伊或干瘪尸体）。19 世纪比较解剖学造词，与 endoskeleton 成对。确切首见年代与首创者不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move outward from the idea of support outside the body: the arthropod shell, the chitin layer, calcareous shells, cast moults, fossils, wearable frames, building frames and a defensive manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「支撑在身体之外」这一想法向外展开：节肢动物硬壳、几丁质层、钙质壳、蜕壳、化石、可穿戴框架、建筑骨架与防御性的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard shell carried on the outside, muscles pulling from within, joints left soft.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具穿在外面的硬壳，肌肉从内侧牵引，关节处保持柔软。

branches.en: THE ARRANGEMENT: support outside, soft tissue inside.
branches.cn: 布局：支撑在外，软组织在内。

branches.en: THE MATERIALS: chitin and calcium carbonate are two ways of hardening the outside.
branches.cn: 材料：几丁质与碳酸钙是硬化外层的两种方式。

branches.en: WHAT IS LEFT: cast shells and fossils are the hard part without the animal.
branches.cn: 留下之物：蜕壳与化石都是失去动物后的硬部。

branches.en: ENGINEERING: wearable frames and building frames copy the load path.
branches.cn: 工程：可穿戴框架与建筑骨架复制了这条受力路径。

branches.en: PROTECTIVE MANNER: a hard outward habit shields something soft.
branches.cn: 防御姿态：坚硬的外在习惯护住柔软之物。

intro.en: Exoskeleton is a Greek-derived compound; the prefix exo-, the base skeleton and the adjective suffix -al all remain productive in English.
intro.cn: exoskeleton 是希腊来源的复合词；前缀 exo-、词基 skeleton 与形容词后缀 -al 在英语中均仍能产词。

latinIntro.en: Greek exō 'outside' gives the prefix exo-, as in exoskeleton and exothermic; Greek skeletos 'dried up' gives skeleton and skeletal.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 exō「外面」给出前缀 exo-，如 exoskeleton、exothermic；希腊 skeletos「干枯的」给出 skeleton 与 skeletal。

items.example: The prefix places the structure outside the body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把结构置于体外。

items.example: The skeleton carries the body's weight.
items.exampleCN: 骨架承担身体的重量。

items.example: The exoskeleton protects the soft body.
items.exampleCN: 外骨骼保护柔软的身体。

items.example: Moulted exoskeletons litter the shore.
items.exampleCN: 蜕下的外骨骼散落岸边。

items.example: Exoskeletal plates overlap like tiles.
items.exampleCN: 外骨骼板像瓦片一样重叠。

items.meaning: by means of an outer skeleton
items.example: The animal is exoskeletally supported.
items.exampleCN: 这种动物靠外骨骼支撑。

items.example: The reaction is exothermic.
items.exampleCN: 这个反应是放热的。

items.meaning: a planet outside the solar system
items.example: An exoplanet passed before its star.
items.exampleCN: 一颗系外行星从它的恒星前经过。

items.example: The exoskeleton suit halved the lifting effort.
items.exampleCN: 外骨骼服把举重费力减半。

definition_zh: 异国风情的；外来的；奇异的；异域情调的
definition_en: coming from a distant country, and therefore striking or strange to local eyes
core_image: 摊位上摆着一堆从未见过的水果，颜色鲜艳得不像本地能长出来的
scene: 旅行者挤进早市，看见一堆从没见过的水果，摊主说是坐船从海的另一边运来的。The stall was piled with exotic fruit that no local customer could name.
sceneCN: 这里 exotic 是「异国风情的、带着异域吸引力的」（第 2 个义项：遥远地方带来的新鲜魅力）；句意：摊上堆满了本地顾客一个也叫不出名字的异国水果。

pos.zh: 形容词：异国风情的；外来的；奇异的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀 -ism 构成，义为「异国情调；异域风格」
由形容词加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「带着异域风情地」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「异域性；奇异感」
由形容词加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使显得有异国风情」

senses.title: Brought from a distant country
senses.titleCN: 来自遥远国度的；外来的
senses.definition: brought from a faraway country and not native to the place where it is found
senses.definitionCN: 从远方带来的，并非被发现之地原产的
senses.example: The cabinet holds a collection of exotic woods sent from the tropics.
senses.exampleCN: 柜子里收藏着一批从热带送来的异国木材。
senses.why: Greek exo means outside, so an exotic thing is first of all a thing whose origin lies outside the known world.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 exo 意为「外面」，所以 exotic 首先指来源在已知世界之外的东西，这是一切用法的起点。

senses.title: Strikingly foreign and appealing
senses.titleCN: 异国风情的；迷人的异域感
senses.definition: carrying the glamour of a distant place, so that it feels fresh, exciting, and slightly unreal
senses.definitionCN: 带着遥远地方的魅力，让人觉得新鲜、兴奋而略不真实
senses.example: Paper lanterns and jars of spice gave the narrow street an exotic charm.
senses.exampleCN: 纸灯笼与一罐罐香料让这条窄街带上一种异域魅力。
senses.why: Distance adds glamour, so the same outside origin becomes a promise of a more colourful life elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 距离会添上魅力，于是「来自外面」这件事本身就成了别处更斑斓生活的许诺，审美义由此从来源义长出来。

senses.title: Strange and slightly unsettling
senses.titleCN: 奇异的；古怪得让人不安
senses.definition: so unusual that it feels odd, unnatural, or hard to place in any familiar category
senses.definitionCN: 异常到让人觉得古怪、不自然或难以归入熟悉类别
senses.example: An exotic smell drifted up from the laboratory drain.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室下水道里飘上一股古怪的气味。
senses.why: What comes from outside can also refuse to fit, and the word keeps that colder edge of strangeness beside the charm.
senses.whyCN: 外来之物也可能怎么都安不进本地秩序，这层「怪」的冷意一直与「迷人」并存，所以同一个词也能表示不安。

senses.title: Not native to a region
senses.definition: of a plant or animal, introduced by human activity into a place where it did not evolve
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物经人类活动被带入并非其演化地的区域
senses.example: Exotic species can crowd out the plants that nesting birds depend on.
senses.exampleCN: 外来物种可能挤掉筑巢鸟类赖以为生的植物。
senses.why: Biology keeps the plain outside sense and drops the glamour, because an introduced species is defined entirely by its origin.
senses.whyCN: 生物学只保留字面上的「外来」，把魅力那一层去掉，因为外来物种的定义正落在来源上，与美不美无关。

senses.title: Unfamiliar in finance
senses.definition: of a currency or financial instrument, unusual in structure and hard for ordinary investors to price
senses.definitionCN: 指货币或金融工具结构少见，普通投资者难以定价
senses.example: Traders moved into exotic currencies once the main markets went quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 主要市场一沉寂，交易员就转向了冷门的外来货币。
senses.why: Finance borrows the word for whatever sits outside the familiar set, so the outside sense survives there in a technical key.
senses.whyCN: 金融界把一切落在熟悉范围之外的东西都叫 exotic，于是「外面」这层意思以术语的形式活了下来。

intro.en: Exotic goes back to the Greek adverb exo, outside, and reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: exotic 可追到希腊语副词 exo（外面），经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

items.en: Exo means outside, and exotikos describes what belongs to another land.
items.cn: exo 意为「在外面」，exotikos 形容属于别国的东西。

items.en: Latin takes exotikos as exoticus, meaning foreign.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 exotikos 借作 exoticus，意为「外来的」。

items.en: French exotique carries the adjective forward with the same sense.
items.cn: 法语 exotique 带着同一含义把形容词往前传。

items.en: English adopts exotic as a plain label for plants, goods, and places from abroad.
items.cn: 英语借入 exotic，最初只是给海外植物、货物与地方贴的标签。

items.en: Travel writing adds the note of glamour, and science later borrows the word for introduced species.
items.cn: 游记文学添上魅力色彩，科学随后又借它指被引入的物种。

note.en: Exotic sits with the Greek outside family and with the ordinary words for foreign and strange.
note.cn: exotic 一边连着希腊语「外面」词族，一边挨着表示「外来的」「奇怪的」普通词。

entries.definition: intended for ordinary people rather than a small circle of experts
entries.definitionCN: 面向普通人的，而非只给少数专家的；与 exotic 同出希腊语「外面」词根，但义为「对外公开的」

entries.definition: the custom of marrying outside your own group
entries.definitionCN: 与族外之人通婚的习俗；exo- 前缀同样表示「外面」

entries.definition: the quality or style of being exotic
entries.definitionCN: 异国情调；刻意追求异域风格的做法

entries.definition: belonging to a country that is not your own
strange in a way that seems to come from far away
not known or not recognised

normalIntro.en: Exotic is built on the Greek word for outside, so the whole family keeps the picture of something carried in from beyond.
normalIntro.cn: exotic 建立在希腊语「外面」这个词上，整个词族都保留「从外面搬进来」的画面。

normal.en: The Greek adverb exo means outside, and the suffix makes an adjective of it.
normal.cn: 希腊语副词 exo 意为「在外面」，加词尾就成了形容词。

normal.en: An exotic fruit is simply one that cannot grow in the local climate.
normal.cn: exotic fruit 就是本地气候里长不出来的水果。

normal.en: Exotic species is the neutral scientific phrase, and the glamour disappears there.
normal.cn: exotic species 是中性的科学说法，魅力那一层在那里消失了。

normal.en: Compare exoteric: same outside root, but it means open to outsiders, not strange.
normal.cn: 对比 exoteric：同一个「外面」词根，但意思是「对外公开的」，并不表示奇怪。

normal.en: Keep exotic for things and places; calling a person exotic can sound like turning them into a curiosity.
normal.cn: exotic 最好用在事物与地方上；用来形容人容易听起来像把人当成猎奇对象。

abstract.en: Picture a crate stamped with a port you cannot find on the map.
abstract.cn: 想象一只木箱，上面盖着一个你在地图上找不到的港口名。

abstract.en: Picture paper lanterns swinging above a street that smells of spice.
abstract.cn: 想象纸灯笼在一条飘着香料味的街上摇晃。

abstract.en: Picture a bird on the fence that no local guidebook lists.
abstract.cn: 想象篱笆上停着一只本地图鉴里查不到的鸟。

examples.en: The shop sells exotic fruit that most customers have never tasted.
examples.cn: 这家店卖大多数顾客从未尝过的异国水果。

examples.en: Critics praised the film for its exotic settings and very slow camera.
examples.cn: 影评人称赞这部片子的异域场景和极慢的镜头。

examples.en: Biologists track exotic plants that escape from garden ponds into rivers.
examples.cn: 生物学家追踪从花园池塘逸出、进入河流的外来植物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「伊格佐提克」，也可拆成「exo（外）+ tic」记成「外面来的」；谐音与拆词只是记忆抓手，并不是词源。

root: 希腊语 exō（在外面）→ exōtikos（外来的）→ 拉丁语 exoticus → 法语 exotique → 英语 exotic，核心义「来自外面的」；同一词根还给出 exoteric 与 exogamy。

sensesIntro.en: Exotic begins as a plain label for what comes from outside, takes on the glamour of distance, keeps a colder sense of strangeness, and then serves biology and finance as a neutral word for the non-native.
sensesIntro.cn: exotic 最初只是「来自外面」的标签，随后带上远方赠予的魅力，又保留「怪异」的冷意，最后在生物学与金融里成为中性的「非本地」术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crate of unknown fruit carried in from a far port.
core.cn: 核心意象：一箱从远方港口运来、叫不出名字的水果。

branches.en: The plain origin sense is the base of the whole word.
branches.cn: 「来源在外面」这个朴素义项是整个词的地基。

branches.en: Glamour grows out of distance, not out of the object itself.
branches.cn: 魅力是从距离里长出来的，不是物体本身自带的。

branches.en: Strangeness is the shadow side of the same outside origin.
branches.cn: 「怪」是同一个「外来」来源投下的影子。

branches.en: Biology and finance both keep only the neutral core of non-native standing.
branches.cn: 生物学与金融都只留下「非本地」这个中性内核。

branches.en: A market stall of imported fruit is literally foreign and charming at once.
branches.cn: 卖进口水果的摊位同时是字面上的「外来」与感觉上的「迷人」。

intro.en: Exotic rests on the Greek adverb exo, outside, and English still keeps the family in exoteric, exogamy, exoticism, and exoticize.
intro.cn: exotic 立在希腊语副词 exo（外面）之上，英语里同族还有 exoteric、exogamy、exoticism 与 exoticize。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed Greek exotikos as exoticus, meaning foreign, and handed it on to French and then English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语 exotikos 借作 exoticus，意为「外来的」，再交给法语，最后进入英语。

items.example: Exō is the outside that the whole family shares.
items.exampleCN: exō 是整个词族共有的那个「外面」。

items.example: Exōtikos describes what belongs to another land.
items.exampleCN: exōtikos 形容属于别国的东西。

items.example: Latin exoticus keeps the same meaning without the glamour.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 exoticus 保留同一含义，还没有魅力色彩。

items.example: French exotique carries the word towards English.
items.exampleCN: 法语 exotique 把词带向英语。

items.example: English exotic adds the note of charm.
items.exampleCN: 英语 exotic 添上了魅力这一层。

items.example: The prefix exo- also appears in exogamy and exoskeleton.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 exo- 还出现在 exogamy 与 exoskeleton 里。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns the Greek stem into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 把希腊语词干变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ism names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 命名这种性质本身。

items.example: The suffix -ally builds the adverb from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ally 由形容词构成副词。

items.example: The suffix -ize makes a verb of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 把形容词变成动词。

definition_en: to become larger in size or amount; to grow in range or business; to give more detail
core_image: 一样东西向四周铺展开、占据更大空间
scene: 加热后金属会明显膨胀，占满缝隙。When heated, the metal will expand and fill the gap.
sceneCN: 这里 expand 是「变大、膨胀」（第 1 个义项）；句意：加热后金属会明显膨胀，占满缝隙。

senses.title: Grow larger
senses.definition: to become larger in size or amount
senses.definitionCN: 在体积或数量上变大
senses.example: Air expands as it warms.
senses.exampleCN: 空气受热会膨胀。
senses.why: The core image is spreading outward.
senses.whyCN: 核心形象是向四周铺展开。

senses.title: Widen range
senses.definition: to grow in range, size, or business
senses.definitionCN: 在范围、规模或业务上扩大
senses.example: The chain expanded to fifty stores.
senses.exampleCN: 这家连锁店扩展到了五十家门店。
senses.why: Physical growth is applied to organizations.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的变大被用于组织扩张。

senses.title: Add detail
senses.definition: to give more detail about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事给出更多细节
senses.example: She expanded on her earlier comment.
senses.exampleCN: 她进一步说明了先前的评论。
senses.why: Spreading outward becomes spreading out an idea.
senses.whyCN: 向外铺开转化为把观点展开。

intro.en: Expand comes from Latin expandere, to spread out.
intro.cn: expand 源自拉丁语 expandere，意为「铺开」。

items.en: Expandere joins ex- (out) with pandere (to spread).
items.cn: expandere 由 ex-（向外）与 pandere（展开）构成。

items.en: Pandere describes spreading something open.
items.cn: pandere 表示把东西铺展开。

items.en: Expansus is the past participle of expandere.
items.cn: expansus 是 expandere 的过去分词。

items.en: Expanden first means to spread out.
items.cn: expanden 最初意为铺展开。

items.en: Expand grows to mean increase in size.
items.cn: expand 逐渐表示体积增大。

items.en: Expand on adds the sense of explaining more.
items.cn: expand on 增加了「进一步解释」之意。

note.en: Expand means to grow larger; expend means to use up.
note.cn: expand 是扩大，expend 则是花费、耗尽。

entries.definition: to use up money or energy
to explain in detail
to think something will happen
to make or become bigger
to make longer or wider
to become larger and rounder

normalIntro.en: Expand is about spreading out and getting bigger.
normalIntro.cn: expand 讲的是铺展开来、变得更大。

normal.en: The balloon expands as you blow into it.
normal.cn: 你一吹气，气球就膨胀起来。

normal.en: The company expanded into three new markets.
normal.cn: 这家公司扩展到了三个新市场。

normal.en: The teacher asked him to expand on his answer.
normal.cn: 老师让他进一步展开回答。

normal.en: Warm air expands and rises.
normal.cn: 暖空气膨胀上升。

normal.en: The library plans to expand its reading room.
normal.cn: 图书馆计划扩建阅览室。

abstract.en: Picture a small circle growing wider.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小圆圈越来越宽。

abstract.en: Imagine a map unfolding across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图在桌上铺展开。

abstract.en: Think of a sponge swelling in water.
abstract.cn: 想象一块海绵在水里胀大。

examples.en: The metal expands when the temperature rises.
examples.cn: 温度升高时金属会膨胀。

examples.en: They hope to expand the program next year.
examples.cn: 他们希望明年扩大这个项目。

examples.en: The bridge design was expanded during the war.
examples.cn: 这座桥的设计在战争期间被扩充了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「expand」里有 ex（向外）+ pand（展开）：向外展开，就是「扩大」。

root: 拉丁语 expandere 由 ex-（向外）与 pandere（展开）构成，核心义「向外铺开」。

sensesIntro.en: Expand means to grow larger, widen a range, or explain in more detail.
sensesIntro.cn: expand 意为变大、扩大范围，或更详细地说明。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something spreading outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物向四周铺展开。

branches.en: Physical spreading is the core sense.
branches.cn: 物理上的铺开是核心义。

branches.en: Growth applies to companies and areas.
branches.cn: 「变大」被用于公司和地区。

branches.en: An idea is spread out with more words.
branches.cn: 观点用更多文字展开。

branches.en: Both involve increase in size or scope.
branches.cn: 两者都涉及体积或范围的增长。

branches.en: Widening scope and adding detail both extend.
branches.cn: 扩大范围与补充细节都是一种延伸。

intro.en: Expand carries the Latin prefix ex- and the verb pandere.
intro.cn: expand 含有拉丁前缀 ex- 与动词 pandere。

latinIntro.en: Latin expandere joins ex- (out) and pandere (to spread).
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 expandere 由 ex-（向外）与 pandere（展开）组合。

items.example: Ex- marks outward movement.
items.exampleCN: ex- 表示向外的动作。

items.example: Pandere gives the idea of spreading.
items.exampleCN: pandere 提供「展开」的含义。

items.example: Expandere is the direct source of expand.
items.exampleCN: expandere 是 expand 的直接来源。

items.example: Expansus supplies the noun stem.
items.exampleCN: expansus 提供名词词干。

items.example: Expand keeps the sense of spreading.
items.exampleCN: expand 保留「铺开」之义。

items.example: -Sion forms the noun expansion.
items.exampleCN: -sion 构成名词 expansion。

items.example: Expansion names the process of growing.
items.exampleCN: expansion 指扩张的过程。

items.example: -Ive forms the adjective expansive.
items.exampleCN: -ive 构成形容词 expansive。

items.example: Expansive describes wide open space.
items.exampleCN: expansive 形容开阔的空间。

latinEntries.exampleCN: pandere 是表示展开的动词。

definition_zh: 可扩展的；可扩容的；可膨胀的；可展开的
definition_en: able to be made larger, wider, or more capable, usually without being replaced
core_image: 一只软壳行李箱，中间的拉链再拉开一层，箱身立刻高出一截
scene: 出门前把行李箱中间的拉链拉开，箱身立刻高出一截，能多塞两件外套。The expandable case took two extra jackets without complaint.
sceneCN: 这里 expandable 是「可扩容的」（第 1 个义项：容量可以被增大）；句意：这只可扩容的箱子又装下了两件外套，毫无吃力。

pos.zh: 形容词：可扩展的；可扩容的；可膨胀的；可展开的

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，由拉丁语「向外摊开」而来，义为「扩大；膨胀；展开」
由动词加名词后缀 -sion 构成，义为「扩张；膨胀；扩展部分」
由动词词干加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「广阔的；扩张的；开朗的」
由 expandable 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可扩展性」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「扩张器；扩展程序」

senses.title: Able to take more capacity
senses.titleCN: 可扩容的；容量可增大的
senses.definition: able to be increased in size, capacity, or scope while keeping the same basic design
senses.definitionCN: 在保持原有基本设计的前提下，体积、容量或范围可以被增大
senses.example: The bag has an expandable section that adds five litres of room.
senses.exampleCN: 这个包有一个可扩容的部分，能多出五升空间。
senses.why: Latin expandere means to spread out, and the suffix adds the idea that the spreading can still be done.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 expandere 意为「摊开」，后缀 -able 再加一层「还来得及这样做」，于是这个词表示「可以被撑大」。

senses.title: Able to swell in volume
senses.definition: able to grow in volume when filled, heated, or put under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在充气、受热或受压时体积能够变大
senses.example: The graft uses an expandable mesh that widens with the artery.
senses.exampleCN: 这例移植用了一种可膨胀的网片，会随动脉一起变宽。
senses.why: The physical sense stays closest to the Latin picture of something spreading outward from inside.
senses.whyCN: 物理义最贴近拉丁语「从里面向外摊开」的画面，是这个词最具体、最可触摸的一层。

senses.title: Able to be unfolded
senses.definition: made of parts that can be opened out from a folded or packed state
senses.definitionCN: 由可以从折叠或收拢状态摊开的部分构成
senses.example: An expandable table hides two leaves under its top.
senses.exampleCN: 一张可展开的桌子在桌面下藏了两块加长板。
senses.why: A folded thing that opens out repeats the same spreading motion, only now inside one object.
senses.whyCN: 折叠之物摊开来，是同一个「向外铺开」的动作缩进一件家具里，所以共用这个词。

senses.title: Able to take extra parts
senses.definition: built so that extra memory, devices, or functions can be added later
senses.definitionCN: 设计上允许日后加装内存、设备或功能
senses.example: Buy an expandable machine if you plan to add drives later.
senses.exampleCN: 如果打算日后加装硬盘，就买一台可扩展的机器。
senses.why: Computing turns capacity into slots, so expandable now means that room for more parts has been left inside.
senses.whyCN: 计算机把「容量」变成插槽，可扩展就是说机身里还留着加装零件的位置，是把容量义技术化了。

intro.en: Expandable joins the Latin verb expandere, to spread out, with the English suffix -able.
intro.cn: expandable 是拉丁语动词 expandere（摊开）加英语后缀 -able 组成的。

items.en: Pandere means to spread, unfold, or open wide.
items.cn: pandere 意为摊开、展开、张阔。

items.en: Expandere joins ex, out, with pandere, to spread, and means to spread out.
items.cn: expandere 由 ex（向外）加 pandere（摊开）组成，意为向外铺开。

items.en: The participle expansus describes something already spread wide.
items.cn: 分词 expansus 描述已经摊得很开的东西。

items.en: Espandre carries the verb into French with the same outward motion.
items.cn: espandre 带着同一个向外动作把动词带进法语。

items.en: English expand appears as a verb meaning to spread out or grow larger.
items.cn: 英语 expand 以动词身份出现，意为铺开或变大。

items.en: The suffix -able is added to expand, so expandable names whatever can be spread or enlarged.
items.cn: 后缀 -able 加在 expand 上，expandable 就指可以被摊开或撑大的东西。

note.en: Expandable belongs to the spreading family of expand and expansion, and sits beside words for things that can be blown up or scaled.
note.cn: expandable 属于 expand、expansion 这一「摊开」词族，旁边则是表示「可充气」「可缩放」的词。

entries.definition: to become larger or to spread out
the act of growing larger or the new part added
able to be used up or given up without loss
entries.definitionCN: 可消耗的；可牺牲的；只是拼写与 expandable 相近，词源不同（来自拉丁语 expendere，付出）

entries.definition: able to be stretched out or added to
able to be filled with air and made bigger
able to grow in size or load without being rebuilt
entries.definitionCN: 可伸缩的；可按规模扩大的

normalIntro.en: Expandable is the adjective of spreading out: the word says that the spreading has not happened yet but can still be done.
normalIntro.cn: expandable 是「摊开」这个动作的形容词：它说的是摊开还没发生，但随时可以做到。

normal.en: Expanding is spreading out, so expandable marks whatever can still be spread wider.
normal.cn: expand 是向外摊开，expandable 就标出还能被摊得更宽的东西。

normal.en: A bag, a table, and a laptop all keep the same picture of extra room.
normal.cn: 一只包、一张桌、一台笔记本，共用的是「还留着余量」这幅画面。

normal.en: Expandable memory is the phrase you meet on laptops and phones.
normal.cn: expandable memory 是笔记本和手机上最常遇到的搭配。

normal.en: Compare expansive: an expansive mood also spreads outward, but nothing is added to it.
normal.cn: 对比 expansive：开朗的心情同样是向外铺开，但并没有增加什么。

normal.en: Do not confuse expandable with expendable, which means able to be used up or given away.
normal.cn: 别把 expandable 和 expendable 弄混，后者意为「可消耗的、可以舍弃的」。

abstract.en: Picture a zip that opens a second compartment behind the first.
abstract.cn: 想象一条拉链，在第一层后面又开出一层。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon drawing breath as it fills and rounds out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只气球一边鼓起来一边像在吸气。

abstract.en: Picture a table leaf swinging up on its hinge and doubling the top.
abstract.cn: 想象一块桌板沿铰链翻起，桌面一下大了一倍。

examples.en: The phone has expandable storage, so a memory card adds room.
examples.cn: 这部手机有可扩展存储，插一张存储卡就能增加空间。

examples.en: An expandable hose shrinks to the size of a lunch box.
examples.cn: 一根可伸缩水管能缩到饭盒那么大。

examples.en: The clinic bought an expandable trailer to serve as a second ward.
examples.cn: 诊所买了一辆可扩展的拖车，用作第二间病房。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「伊克斯潘德波」，可拆成「ex（向外）+ pand（摊开）+ able（能）」，记成「能向外摊开的」；谐音只是记忆抓手，并不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ pandere（摊开）→ expandere（向外铺开）→ 古法语 espandre → 英语 expand；再加后缀 -able 得 expandable，核心义「能被摊大」。

sensesIntro.en: Expandable keeps one physical image of opening outward, then applies it to capacity, to swelling, to unfolded objects, and finally to machines that leave room for more parts.
sensesIntro.cn: expandable 只守着「向外张开」这一个画面，再把它依次用到容量、膨胀、摊开的物件，最后用到留出加装位置的机器上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a zip opened to reveal a second layer still folded inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：拉开一条拉链，露出里面还折着的第二层。

branches.en: Extra capacity is the everyday sense of the word.
branches.cn: 「还装得下更多」是最日常的义项。

branches.en: Swelling keeps the motion inside the material itself.
branches.cn: 膨胀把这个动作收进材料内部，是同一画面的物理版本。

branches.en: Unfolding turns the spreading into a single object opening out.
branches.cn: 展开把「铺开」变成一件物件自己张开。

branches.en: Computing turns capacity into empty slots for later parts.
branches.cn: 计算机把容量变成留给日后零件的空插槽。

branches.en: A bigger bag and an opened table both promise room that was there all along.
branches.cn: 更能装的包与摊开的桌子，许诺的都是「本来就在那里的余量」。

intro.en: Expandable is a transparent build: the Latin prefix ex-, the Latin verb pandere, and the English suffix -able.
intro.cn: expandable 的构词非常透明：拉丁语前缀 ex-、拉丁语动词 pandere，再加英语后缀 -able。

latinIntro.en: Latin pandere means to spread or unfold, and expandere puts that spreading outward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pandere 意为摊开、展开，expandere 则把这个摊开朝外做出去。

items.example: The prefix ex- points the spreading away from the centre.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把这场摊开指向远离中心的方向。

items.example: Pandere is the motion at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: pandere 是这个词心脏处的那个动作。

items.example: Expandere is the direct source of expand.
items.exampleCN: expandere 是 expand 的直接来源。

items.example: Expansus feeds the English adjective expansive.
items.exampleCN: expansus 供给了英语形容词 expansive。

items.example: Espandre carries the verb through French.
items.exampleCN: espandre 把这个动词经法语传下去。

items.meaning: to grow larger or spread out
items.example: Expand keeps both the physical and the figurative motion.
items.exampleCN: expand 同时保留物理与比喻两种动作。

items.example: The suffix -able turns the verb into a possibility.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把动词变成一种可能性。

items.example: The suffix -sion names the act and its result.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -sion 命名这一动作及其结果。

items.example: The suffix -ive describes the spreading quality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 描述「向外铺开」的性质。

items.example: The suffix -ity names the quality of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 命名该形容词的性质。

definition_en: the process of becoming larger; growth in business or territory; a fuller development of an idea
core_image: 版图或体积不断向外扩大的过程
scene: 这家企业的快速扩张带来了数千个岗位。The rapid expansion of the firm created thousands of jobs.
sceneCN: 这里 expansion 是「扩张、扩展」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这家企业的快速扩张带来了数千个岗位。

senses.title: Growth in size
senses.definition: the process of becoming larger in size or volume
senses.definitionCN: 体积或容量变大的过程
senses.example: Thermal expansion can crack the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 热膨胀可能使玻璃开裂。
senses.why: The noun names the process behind expand.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指 expand 背后的过程。

senses.title: Business growth
senses.definition: growth in business, territory, or influence
senses.definitionCN: 业务、领土或影响力上的增长
senses.example: The expansion of the network took five years.
senses.exampleCN: 网络的扩张花了五年时间。
senses.why: Physical growth is applied to organizations and land.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的扩大被用于组织和土地。

senses.title: Added detail
senses.definition: a fuller development of an idea in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在口头或书面中把观点充分展开
senses.example: The essay needs an expansion of its main argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章需要把主要论点展开。
senses.why: Spreading outward becomes spreading out an argument.
senses.whyCN: 向外铺开转化为把论点展开。

intro.en: Expansion comes from Latin expansio, a spreading out.
intro.cn: expansion 源自拉丁语 expansio，意为「铺展开」。

items.en: Expansio is the noun for a spreading out.
items.cn: expansio 是表示铺开的名词。

items.en: It comes from expandere, to spread open.
items.cn: 它来自 expandere，意为铺展开。

items.en: Expansus supplies the participle stem.
items.cn: expansus 提供分词词干。

items.en: Expansioun names the act of spreading.
items.cn: expansioun 指铺开的动作。

items.en: Expansion covers growth of land and trade.
items.cn: expansion 涵盖土地与贸易的增长。

items.en: Expansion also names added detail in writing.
items.cn: expansion 还指写作中的展开补充。

note.en: Expansion is growth; expense is money spent.
note.cn: expansion 是扩张，expense 则是开支。

entries.definition: a wide area of land or space
money spent on something
the size or range of something
the process of growing
the act of making something longer or wider
the act of making something bigger

normalIntro.en: Expansion is the noun for growing or spreading.
normalIntro.cn: expansion 是表示扩大或铺开的名词。

normal.en: The expansion of the airport began last spring.
normal.cn: 机场的扩建去年春天开工。

normal.en: Thermal expansion explains the loose lid.
normal.cn: 热膨胀可以解释盖子为何变松。

normal.en: The company funded its expansion with a loan.
normal.cn: 公司靠贷款为扩张提供资金。

normal.en: His expansion of the theory filled three pages.
normal.cn: 他对该理论的展开写了三页。

normal.en: Economic expansion brought new jobs to the town.
normal.cn: 经济扩张给小镇带来了新工作。

abstract.en: Picture a map quietly growing at its edges.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图的边缘悄悄向外延伸。

abstract.en: Imagine a circle widening on still water.
abstract.cn: 想象静水面上一个圆圈不断扩大。

abstract.en: Think of a story that keeps adding chapters.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不断添加章节的故事。

examples.en: The expansion of the railway changed the region.
examples.cn: 铁路的扩张改变了这个地区。

examples.en: Heat causes the expansion of the metal bar.
examples.cn: 热量使金属棒膨胀。

examples.en: The report offers a detailed expansion of the plan.
examples.cn: 这份报告对计划作了详细展开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「expansion」是 expand（扩大）的名词形式，-sion 表示动作或结果。

root: 拉丁语 expansio（展开）来自 expandere，表示「向外铺开」的动作与结果。

sensesIntro.en: Expansion means growth in size, growth in business or land, or a fuller development of an idea.
sensesIntro.cn: expansion 意为体积增大、业务或领土扩张，或观点的展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an area or volume pushing outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：面积或体积不断向外扩。

branches.en: The process of growing larger is the base.
branches.cn: 变大的过程是基础义。

branches.en: Growing is applied to business and land.
branches.cn: 「变大」被用于业务与土地。

branches.en: An argument is spread out in more detail.
branches.cn: 论点被更详细地展开。

branches.en: Both are forms of increase and extension.
branches.cn: 两者都是增长与延伸。

branches.en: Wider scope and added detail both expand ideas.
branches.cn: 扩大范围与补充细节都在扩展观点。

intro.en: Expansion builds on Latin expandere with the suffix -sion.
intro.cn: expansion 在拉丁语 expandere 基础上加后缀 -sion。

latinIntro.en: Latin expansio and expandere supply the core forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 expansio 与 expandere 提供核心词形。

items.example: Ex- signals spreading outward.
items.exampleCN: ex- 表示向外铺开。

items.example: Pandere gives the spreading root.
items.exampleCN: pandere 提供「展开」词根。

items.example: Expandere is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: expandere 是基础动词。

items.example: Expansio is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: expansio 是直接来源。

items.example: -Sion forms nouns from verbs.
items.exampleCN: -sion 把动词变为名词。

items.example: Expansion names the process.
items.exampleCN: expansion 指这一过程。

items.example: Expand is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: expand 是名词背后的动词。

items.example: -Ive forms expansive.
items.exampleCN: -ive 构成 expansive。

items.example: Expansive describes open space.
items.exampleCN: expansive 描述开阔空间。

definition_zh: 期待；盼望；预期；预期寿命
definition_en: the state of expecting something to happen, or the length of time something is likely to last
core_image: 候诊室里一排人坐着，眼睛都盯着那扇还没开的门
scene: 候诊室里一排人坐着，眼睛全盯着那扇还没开的门，空气里都是等待。Nobody spoke, and the expectancy in the room was almost loud.
sceneCN: 这里 expectancy 是「期待的情绪」（第 1 个义项：紧张盼着某事发生的心情）；句意：没人说话，屋里的期待几乎响得出来。

pos.zh: 名词：期待；盼望；预期；预期寿命

collocations.zh: 在期待之中；有待继承（法律用语）

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「预料；期待；等待」
由动词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「期望；预期」
由拉丁语现在分词词干构成，义为「期待的；怀孕的」
由 expectant 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「满怀期待地」

senses.title: The tense state of waiting
senses.definition: a feeling of tense waiting, when something is expected to happen very soon
senses.definitionCN: 紧张等待的心情，觉得某事马上就要发生
senses.example: A hush of expectancy fell over the hall before the winner was named.
senses.exampleCN: 宣布获奖者之前，礼堂里落下一种期待的静默。
senses.why: Latin exspectare means to look out for, so expectancy is the state of keeping your eyes on what should come.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 exspectare 意为「向外张望、守候」，所以 expectancy 就是眼睛一直盯着那个「该来的东西」的状态。

senses.title: A calculated expectation
senses.definition: an estimate of how much or how long something will happen, based on evidence rather than feeling
senses.definitionCN: 依据证据而非情绪，对某事发生多少或持续多久作出的估计
senses.example: The survey puts the expectancy of rain at seventy percent.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把降雨的预期概率定在七成。
senses.why: The waiting stare becomes a number once data can say what usually follows, so the same noun names an estimate.
senses.whyCN: 一旦数据能说出通常会出现什么，那种「张望」就变成了数字，于是同一个名词也能指估计值。

senses.title: Length of life expected
senses.definition: the number of years a person or group is likely to live, usually given as an average
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体可能存活的年数，通常以平均值给出
senses.example: Life expectancy in the region has risen by nine years since the clinic opened.
senses.exampleCN: 自诊所开设以来，该地区的预期寿命提高了九年。
senses.why: The phrase life expectancy fixes the general estimate onto the one quantity everyone watches, namely how long a life lasts.
senses.whyCN: life expectancy 把这个笼统的「预期」钉到人人都在看的一个量上，也就是寿命长短，所以 expectancy 单独用也能指预期寿命。

senses.title: A legal interest still to come
senses.titleCN: （法律）期待权；将来可得的利益
senses.definition: a right or property interest that a person will receive in the future if a stated condition is met
senses.definitionCN: 在特定条件满足后，某人将来可以取得的权利或财产利益
senses.example: The heir sold his expectancy before the will was read.
senses.exampleCN: 继承人在遗嘱宣读之前就把自己的期待权卖掉了。
senses.why: Law keeps the pure forward-looking core: the right exists only as something still looked forward to.
senses.whyCN: 法律保留了「朝前看」这个最纯的内核：这项权利此刻只以「将来会有」的形式存在。

intro.en: Expectancy comes from Latin exspectare, to look out for, built on spectare, to watch.
intro.cn: expectancy 来自拉丁语 exspectare（向外张望、守候），其底层是 spectare（看）。

items.en: Spectare means to look at or watch, and gives English spectator and inspect.
items.cn: spectare 意为观看、注视，也给出英语的 spectator 与 inspect。

items.en: Exspectare joins ex, out, with spectare, to watch, and means to look out for something.
items.cn: exspectare 由 ex（向外）加 spectare（看）组成，意为向外张望、等着某物出现。

items.en: The noun exspectantia names a state of waiting for something to arrive.
items.cn: 名词 exspectantia 指等候某物到来的状态。

items.en: Medieval legal and church writing keeps expectantia alive as a word for what is due in future.
items.cn: 中世纪的法律与教会文书让 expectantia 存活下来，指将来应得之物。

items.en: English adopts expectancy as a noun for the state of expecting.
items.cn: 英语借入 expectancy，作名词表示期待的状态。

items.en: The fixed phrase life expectancy turns the noun into a measure of years.
items.cn: 固定短语 life expectancy 把这个名词变成以年计的量度。

note.en: Expectancy is the state noun of the expect family, and it stands close to words for looking ahead.
note.cn: expectancy 是 expect 词族里表示「状态」的名词，站位靠近一批表示「往前看」的词。

entries.definition: to think that something will happen
a belief that something will happen
entries.definitionCN: 期望；预期；期待中的事物

entries.definition: waiting for something with hope or tension
the act of expecting something and getting ready for it
the possibility that something good will happen
a forecast of what is likely to happen

normalIntro.en: Expectancy is expect plus a suffix that names a state, so the word is the condition of standing with your eyes on the door.
normalIntro.cn: expectancy 是 expect 加一个表示「状态」的后缀，所以这个词就是「站着把眼睛放在门上」的那个状态。

normal.en: Expect carries the watching root spect, the same one in spectator and inspect.
normal.cn: expect 里带着表示「看」的词根 spect，spectator 与 inspect 用的是同一个。

normal.en: The suffix -ancy names a state, so expectancy is the state rather than the thing expected.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ancy 命名一种状态，所以 expectancy 指状态，而不指被期待的那件事。

normal.en: Learn life expectancy first: it is the phrase that carries the word through exams.
normal.cn: 先记 life expectancy，考试里几乎都是靠这个搭配把这个词带出来。

normal.en: Expectation is the everyday noun; expectancy is narrower and often statistical or legal.
normal.cn: expectation 是日常名词；expectancy 范围更窄，常带统计或法律色彩。

normal.en: A look of expectancy is tense, not calm hope, so keep the waiting edge in mind.
normal.cn: a look of expectancy 是绷着的，不是安然盼望，要记住这层「等」的紧张。

abstract.en: Picture a row of faces all turned towards a door that has not opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一排脸全都转向那扇还没开的门。

abstract.en: Picture a chart with a rising line and one number printed beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张图，线在往上走，旁边印着一个数字。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler marked in years, with a pencil mark where the line is expected to stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一把以年为刻度的尺，有人用铅笔标出这条线预计停在哪里。

examples.en: Life expectancy for the group rose sharply after clean water arrived.
examples.cn: 干净水源接通之后，这一群体的预期寿命大幅上升。

examples.en: There was a nervous expectancy in the crowd before the result was read out.
examples.cn: 结果宣读出之前，人群里有一种紧张的期待。

examples.en: The law treats a future inheritance as an expectancy, not as property.
examples.cn: 法律把将来的继承视为一种期待权，而不是既有财产。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「伊克斯派克坦西」，可拆成「ex（向外）+ spect（看）+ ancy（状态）」，记成「一直朝外看的状态」；谐音只是记忆抓手，并不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ spectare（看）→ exspectare（向外张望、守候）→ 晚期拉丁语 exspectantia（等候的状态）→ 英语 expectancy，核心义「朝外张望，等它到来」。

sensesIntro.en: Expectancy starts as the tense state of watching for something, narrows into a calculated estimate, is fixed by life expectancy onto years of life, and survives in law as a right still to come.
sensesIntro.cn: expectancy 先是「朝外张望、等它来」的紧张状态，再收窄为基于数据的估计，又被 life expectancy 钉到寿命年数上，最后在法律里保留「将来才到手」的权利义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of people watching a door that has not opened yet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排人盯着那扇还没打开的门。

branches.en: The waiting state is the sense the word was born with.
branches.cn: 「等着」这个状态是这个词与生俱来的义项。

branches.en: A calculated estimate is the same waiting turned into data.
branches.cn: 基于数据的预期，是同一种等待被换算成了数字。

branches.en: Years of life are the one quantity the phrase life expectancy always measures.
branches.cn: 寿命年数是 life expectancy 这个搭配永远在量的那个量。

branches.en: Law keeps only the forward-looking skeleton of the word.
branches.cn: 法律只留下这个词「朝前看」的骨架。

branches.en: The tense hush and the printed figure are two ends of one expectation.
branches.cn: 绷紧的静默与印出的数字，是同一个「预期」的两端。

intro.en: Expectancy is built from the Latin prefix ex-, the Latin verb spectare, and the noun suffix -ancy.
intro.cn: expectancy 由拉丁语前缀 ex-、拉丁语动词 spectare 与名词后缀 -ancy 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin spectare means to watch, and exspectare means to watch out for something until it comes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spectare 意为注视，exspectare 意为一直朝外看，直到那件东西出现。

items.example: The prefix ex- sends the watching outward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把这场注视送向外面。

items.example: Spectare also gives spectator and spectacle.
items.exampleCN: spectare 还给出 spectator 与 spectacle。

items.meaning: to look out for, wait for
items.example: Exspectare is the direct source of expect.
items.exampleCN: exspectare 是 expect 的直接来源。

items.example: Exspectantia turns the waiting into a noun.
items.exampleCN: exspectantia 把「等」这个动作变成名词。

items.example: Expect keeps the forward look of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: expect 保留了拉丁语动词「朝前看」的方向。

items.example: The suffix -ancy names the state rather than the act.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ancy 命名状态，而不是动作。

items.meaning: a belief that something will happen
items.example: The suffix -ation names the act and its content.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 命名动作及其内容。

items.example: The suffix -ant describes the person who waits.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 描述正在等待的人。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词。
