items.exampleCN: 词根 -spect- 还出现在 inspect 与 respect 里。

definition_en: a belief that something will happen; a hope or requirement; the standards people expect you to meet
core_image: 心里悬着一个「应该会发生」的念头
scene: 她的表现远远超出了大家的预期。Her performance went far beyond everyone's expectation.
sceneCN: 这里 expectation 是「预期、期望」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她的表现远远超出了大家的预期。

senses.title: Belief about the future
senses.definition: a belief that something will happen
senses.definitionCN: 相信某事将会发生的看法
senses.example: The result was beyond our expectation.
senses.exampleCN: 结果超出了我们的预期。
senses.why: The noun names the belief itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指这种信念本身。

senses.title: Hope or requirement
senses.definition: a strong hope that something will happen
senses.definitionCN: 强烈希望某事发生
senses.example: She has high expectations for her students.
senses.exampleCN: 她对学生们抱有很高的期望。
senses.why: Belief becomes a wish or a demand.
senses.whyCN: 信念变成愿望或要求。

senses.title: Standards to meet
senses.definition: the standards that people expect you to meet
senses.definitionCN: 人们期待你达到的标准
senses.example: He struggled to meet the expectations of the job.
senses.exampleCN: 他努力想达到这份工作的要求。
senses.why: A hope hardens into a social standard.
senses.whyCN: 希望固化为社会标准。

intro.en: Expectation comes from Latin exspectatio, a looking out for.
intro.cn: expectation 源自拉丁语 exspectatio，意为「向外张望、等候」。

items.en: Exspectatio is the noun of exspectare.
items.cn: exspectatio 是 exspectare 的名词形式。

items.en: Exspectare means to look out for something.
items.cn: exspectare 意为留意等候某事。

items.en: Expectacion keeps the sense of waiting.
items.cn: expectacion 保留等候的含义。

items.en: Expectacioun names a looking forward.
items.cn: expectacioun 指向前张望。

items.en: Expectation adds the sense of a demand.
items.cn: expectation 增加了「要求」之义。

items.en: Expectations often means standards to meet.
items.cn: expectations 常指需要达到的标准。

note.en: Expectation is what you believe will happen; an exception is something left out.
note.cn: expectation 是你相信会发生的事，exception 则是例外。

entries.definition: a case not included in a rule
an organized journey
special skill or knowledge
a wish for something good
the act of expecting something
a view of what may happen

normalIntro.en: Expectation is the noun for what you think will happen.
normalIntro.cn: expectation 是表示「你认为会发生什么」的名词。

normal.en: The film exceeded all our expectations.
normal.cn: 这部电影超出了我们所有的预期。

normal.en: Parents often place high expectations on children.
normal.cn: 父母常对孩子寄予厚望。

normal.en: Against all expectations, the team won.
normal.cn: 出乎所有人意料，这支队伍赢了。

normal.en: The new restaurant did not meet expectations.
normal.cn: 这家新餐厅没有达到预期。

normal.en: Her expectation of a quiet evening was ruined.
normal.cn: 她想要安静夜晚的期望落空了。

abstract.en: Picture a closed box you believe is full.
abstract.cn: 想象一个你相信装满东西的盒子。

abstract.en: Imagine a path that leads to a guessed door.
abstract.cn: 想象一条通往猜测之门的道路。

abstract.en: Think of a score card waiting to be filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一张等着填分的记分卡。

examples.en: The quality of the meal went beyond expectation.
examples.cn: 这顿饭的品质超出了预期。

examples.en: She had little expectation of winning the prize.
examples.cn: 她几乎没指望能得奖。

examples.en: The job failed to meet his expectations.
examples.cn: 这份工作没能达到他的期望。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「expectation」由 expect（期待）加 -ation 构成：期待这件事本身，就是「预期」。

root: 拉丁语 exspectare（向外张望、等候）的名词形式 exspectatio 进入英语，核心义「所期待之事」。

sensesIntro.en: Expectation means a belief about the future, a hope, or the standards others set for you.
sensesIntro.cn: expectation 意为对未来的预期、一种希望，或他人为你设定的标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thought fixed on a coming result.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个念头锁定在即将到来的结果上。

branches.en: The base sense is a belief about the future.
branches.cn: 基础义是对未来的信念。

branches.en: The belief becomes a strong hope.
branches.cn: 信念变成强烈的希望。

branches.en: The hope becomes a standard to meet.
branches.cn: 希望变成需达到的标准。

branches.en: Prediction and hope share one forward look.
branches.cn: 预测与希望共享同一种向前看。

branches.en: Personal hope and social standard are linked.
branches.cn: 个人希望与社会标准相互关联。

intro.en: Expectation adds the noun suffix -ation to expect.
intro.cn: expectation 在 expect 后加名词后缀 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Latin exspectare and exspectatio are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exspectare 与 exspectatio 是来源词形。

items.example: Ex- marks looking outward.
items.exampleCN: ex- 表示向外张望。

items.example: Spectare gives the watching root.
items.exampleCN: spectare 提供「观看」词根。

items.example: Exspectare is the source verb.
items.exampleCN: exspectare 是来源动词。

items.example: Exspectatio gives English expectation.
items.exampleCN: exspectatio 演变为英语 expectation。

items.example: -Ation builds abstract nouns.
items.exampleCN: -ation 构成抽象名词。

items.example: Expectation names the belief.
items.exampleCN: expectation 指这一信念。

items.example: Expect is the verb base.
items.exampleCN: expect 是动词词基。

items.example: Expectant adds the adjective suffix.
items.exampleCN: expectant 加上了形容词词尾。

definition_zh: 远征；探险；考察旅行；探险队；远征队
definition_en: a long organized journey made to explore or study a distant place, or the group of people who make it
core_image: 一队人背着行囊，从熟悉的村口走向地图上的空白处
scene: 十九世纪的博物学者带着仪器和骡子，向内陆的空白地带出发。In the nineteenth century, the expedition set out for the blank spaces on the map.
sceneCN: 这里 expedition 是「远征、探险考察」（第 1 个义项：为探索某地而组织的长途旅行）；句意：十九世纪的博物学者带着仪器和骡子，向内陆的空白地带出发。

pos.zh: 远征；探险；考察旅行；探险队；远征队

derivatives.zh: 由 expedition 加 -ary 构成，义为「远征的；探险的」
同出拉丁 expedire，义为「加快；促成」
由 expedite 加 -ious 构成，义为「迅速而有效的」
同出 expedire 的「使便利」义，义为「权宜的；得计的」

senses.title: A long journey made to explore a place
senses.definition: a long organized journey to a distant place, made in order to explore it or to study something there
senses.definitionCN: 为探索或研究某地而组织的长途旅行
senses.example: The expedition spent four months mapping the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这支探险队花了四个月为那条河绘制地图。
senses.why: Latin expedire meant to free the feet from a snare, so the journey is a setting loose of feet toward open ground.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 expedire 意为把脚从罗网中解开，所以这场远行就是让双脚脱困、走向开阔地。

senses.title: The group that makes such a journey
senses.definition: the team of people, animals, and equipment sent on such a journey
senses.definitionCN: 为这类远行而组织起来的人员、牲畜与装备
senses.example: The whole expedition was flown home after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，整支队伍被空运回国。
senses.why: Because the journey must be planned and staffed, the word slides from the trip to the team that undertakes it.
senses.whyCN: 由于这类远行必须有人筹划、有人出人，词义就从「旅程」滑向承担旅程的那支队伍。

senses.title: A military campaign abroad
senses.definition: a military campaign sent to a distant country, especially in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 派往远方国家的军事行动，尤见于较早的用法
senses.example: The Roman expedition pushed north through the forests.
senses.exampleCN: 罗马的远征军穿过森林向北推进。
senses.why: Latin expeditio was the ordinary word for a campaign, because troops were dispatched to act at once.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 expeditio 本是「出征」的常用词，因为军队一旦派出就要立刻行动。

senses.title: A short trip with a set purpose
senses.definition: a short trip made for a particular purpose, often practical or pleasant
senses.definitionCN: 为某个具体目的而进行的短途出行，常带实用或消遣色彩
senses.example: We made a shopping expedition to the market.
senses.exampleCN: 我们专程去市场采购了一趟。
senses.why: The purpose-driven journey shrinks from continents to a single afternoon without changing its shape.
senses.whyCN: 「为目标而出发」这个形状不变，只是尺度从跨越大陆缩到一个下午。

senses.title: Promptness in acting
senses.definition: speed or promptness in doing something, now mostly in formal phrases
senses.definitionCN: 做事的速度与利落，现多用于正式短语
senses.example: The matter was settled with expedition.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事被迅速处理完毕。
senses.why: The root sense of being unencumbered turns into acting without delay.
senses.whyCN: 词根里「无所牵绊」的意思，转成了办事不耽搁。

senses.title: An organized inquiry into a subject
senses.definition: an organized attempt to explore an unfamiliar subject or field of knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 对陌生课题或知识领域所作的有组织的探索
senses.example: Their expedition into local history took ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对本地历史的探索持续了十年。
senses.why: Exploring ground and exploring records use the same outward movement of attention.
senses.whyCN: 踏勘土地与翻查档案，用的是同一种向外伸出的注意力。

intro.en: Expedition comes from Latin expeditio, a setting in order and later a campaign, from expedire, to free the feet.
intro.cn: expedition 来自拉丁语 expeditio（整备，后指出征），源自动词 expedire（把脚解开）。

items.en: Expedire joins ex-, out, and pes, foot: to free the feet from a snare, hence to set free or get ready.
items.cn: expedire 由 ex-（向外）与 pes（脚）合成，本指把脚从罗网中解开，引申为「使脱身、使就绪」。

items.en: The noun expeditio first means a setting in order, then a military campaign.
items.cn: 名词 expeditio 先指「整备、安排」，再指「出征」。

items.en: Expedicion carries the campaign sense into French.
items.cn: expedicion 把「出征」这一义项带入法语。

items.en: Expedicioun appears in English for a campaign fought abroad.
items.cn: 中古英语 expedicioun 指在海外进行的军事行动。

items.en: Travellers and naturalists apply the word to journeys of exploration.
items.cn: 十七世纪的旅行者与博物学者把这个词用在探险旅行上。

items.en: Modern English uses it for polar, scientific, and even shopping trips.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指极地考察、科学考察，甚至购物之行。

note.en: Expedition belongs to the Latin family of freeing the feet, next to expedite and expeditious, and to the ordinary words for long journeys.
note.cn: expedition 属于拉丁语「把脚放开」的词族，与 expedite、expeditious 相邻，也与表示长途旅行的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: to make a process happen sooner or faster
done quickly and efficiently
belonging to or forming a military expedition
an act of travelling from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 从一地到另一地的旅行

entries.definition: a long journey by sea or through space
entries.definitionCN: 海上或太空中的长途航行

entries.definition: a long and difficult walk, often in rough country
entries.definitionCN: 在崎岖地带进行的长途艰苦步行

normalIntro.en: Expedition keeps the Latin picture of feet freed for the road, and the same root runs through expedite.
normalIntro.cn: expedition 保留了拉丁语「把脚放开、好上路」的画面，同一个词根也贯穿 expedite。

normal.en: Ex- means out and pes means foot, so an expedition is a going out on foot.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex- 表示「向外」，词根 pes 表示「脚」，所以 expedition 就是「走出去」。

normal.en: Go on an expedition is the usual verb phrase.
normal.cn: 常用搭配是「go on an expedition」，表示「去探险」。

normal.en: A research expedition is sent out to gather data.
normal.cn: 「a research expedition」指被派出去收集数据的科学考察。

normal.en: Expedite, from the same root, means to hurry a process along.
normal.cn: 同根的 expedite 表示把某个流程加快。

normal.en: With expedition is a formal way to say quickly.
normal.cn: 「with expedition」是「迅速地」的正式说法。

abstract.en: Picture a line of loaded mules leaving the last village behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一队驮着行李的骡子离开最后一个村庄。

abstract.en: Picture the same line as one body: people, tents, and instruments moving together.
abstract.cn: 想象同一支队伍像一个整体：人、帐篷与仪器一起移动。

abstract.en: Picture soldiers marching in step with packs and banners.
abstract.cn: 想象士兵背着行囊、打着旗帜齐步前进。

examples.en: The expedition reached the coast after three months.
examples.cn: 这支探险队在三个月后抵达海岸。

examples.en: She joined a research expedition to the Arctic.
examples.cn: 她加入了一支前往北极的科学考察队。

examples.en: The contract was signed with expedition.
examples.cn: 合同被迅速签署。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「伊克斯佩迪申」——听上去像一队人被派去很远的地方，这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语「expedire」（把脚从罗网中解开、使脱身）＝「ex-」（向外）+「pes/ped-」（脚），过去分词「expeditus」意为「准备就绪」；名词「expeditio」先指「整备、出征」，后泛指远行与考察。

sensesIntro.en: Expedition starts as an organized setting-out, widens to any purposeful journey and the team that makes it, and ends with speed itself.
sensesIntro.cn: expedition 从「有组织的出发」开始，扩展为任何有目的的远行以及执行远行的队伍，最后还长出「迅速」这一义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet freed from a snare and pointed at open ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：双脚从罗网中解脱，朝向开阔地。

branches.en: The purposeful long journey is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 有目的的长途远行是主要的现代义项。

branches.en: The team takes its name from the journey it undertakes.
branches.cn: 队伍从它所承担的那场远行得名。

branches.en: The military campaign is the oldest recorded sense.
branches.cn: 军事出征是有记录的最早义项。

branches.en: A shopping trip and a study of the past are the same purpose-driven journey at two scales.
branches.cn: 购物之行与对历史的钻研，是同一个「为目标而出发」在两种尺度上的样子。

branches.en: Speed grows out of the idea of moving without hindrance.
branches.cn: 「迅速」这一义项由「行动无所阻碍」的观念生长出来。

intro.en: Expedition is built on the Latin verb expedire, with the noun ending -tion and the adjective ending -ary around it.
intro.cn: expedition 建立在拉丁动词 expedire 之上，周围配着名词词尾 -tion 与形容词词尾 -ary。

latinIntro.en: Latin expedire means to free the feet from a snare, and expeditio means a campaign.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 expedire 意为把脚从罗网中解开，expeditio 意为出征。

items.example: The prefix ex- opens both expedition and expel.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 同时开启 expedition 与 expel 的词义。

items.example: The root ped- supplies the image of feet in expedition.
items.exampleCN: 词根 ped- 为 expedition 提供「脚」的意象。

items.meaning: to free the feet, to make ready
items.meaningCN: 解开脚上的束缚；使就绪
items.example: Expedire is the verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: expedire 是整个词族背后的动词。

items.meaning: a setting in order, a campaign
items.example: Expeditio is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: expeditio 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 动作或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -tion turns expeditio into expedition.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 把 expeditio 变成 expedition。

items.meaning: a purposeful journey, or the team that makes it
items.meaningCN: 有目的的远行；执行远行的队伍
items.example: Expedition keeps both the journey and the team.
items.exampleCN: expedition 同时保留「旅程」与「队伍」两个意思。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms expeditionary.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 构成 expeditionary。

items.example: Expeditionary describes a force sent far from home.
items.exampleCN: expeditionary 描述被派往远方的部队。

items.example: Expedite keeps the old sense of removing obstacles.
items.exampleCN: expedite 保留了「清除阻碍」的旧义。

items.example: Expeditious adds the adjective ending -ious.
items.exampleCN: expeditious 加了形容词词尾 -ious。

latinEntries.meaning: to free the feet, to set in order

definition_en: to force a person to leave a place, school, or country, or to force something out of a container or the body
core_image: 一只手把一个人推出门外，门随即在身后合上
scene: 校董事会投票决定把那名学生开除出校。The school board voted to expel the student.
sceneCN: 这里 expel 是「开除、除名」（第 1 个义项：把成员强制逐出学校或组织）；句意：校董事会投票决定开除这名学生。

derivatives.zh: 由 expel 的拉丁分词词干加 -sion 构成，义为「驱逐；开除」
由 expel 加 -ee 构成，指「被驱逐者」
由 expulsion 加 -ive 构成，义为「排出的；逐出的」

senses.title: To force a member out of a school or group
senses.definition: to officially force a student or member to leave a school, club, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 正式强制学生或成员离开学校、俱乐部或组织
senses.example: Two pupils were expelled for cheating.
senses.exampleCN: 两名学生因作弊被开除。
senses.why: The Latin verb drives a person out; the school sense keeps that outward push, only the door is now institutional.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词是把人往外赶，学校义项保留同样的向外推力，只是那道门变成了制度之门。

senses.title: To send a foreign national out of a country
senses.definition: to order a foreigner to leave a country, usually by force of law
senses.definitionCN: 通常依据法律强制外国人离开本国
senses.example: The embassy staff were expelled within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 使馆人员在一周内被驱逐出境。
senses.why: A border is a doorway on a national scale, and expelling is pushing someone through it.
senses.whyCN: 国界是国家尺度上的一道门口，驱逐就是把某人从这道门口推出去。

senses.title: To push gas or liquid out of the body
senses.definition: to force air, smoke, or liquid out of the lungs, a pipe, or another container
senses.definitionCN: 把空气、烟或液体从肺、管道或其他容器中压出
senses.example: The engine expels hot gas through the rear pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机通过后部管道排出热气。
senses.why: The same outward push now works on matter instead of people.
senses.whyCN: 同样的向外推力，作用对象由人换成了物质。

senses.title: To drive someone physically out of a place
senses.definition: to force a person to leave a room or building by pushing or threatening
senses.definitionCN: 用推搡或威胁迫使某人离开房间或建筑
senses.example: The guards expelled the demonstrators from the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 保安把示威者赶出了大厅。
senses.why: This is the plainest physical reading of the root: hands on a body, and the body through a door.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根最直白的物理读法：双手落在身上，身体被推过门口。

senses.title: To send a player off the field
senses.definition: to order a player to leave the field for a serious foul
senses.definitionCN: 因严重犯规而命令球员离开场地
senses.example: The referee expelled him after the second foul.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次犯规之后，裁判把他罚出场。
senses.why: A pitch has boundaries like a room, so the old pushing-out image fits sport without any change.
senses.whyCN: 球场和房间一样有边界，所以「往外推」的老意象原样适用于体育。

senses.title: To rid the mind of something
senses.definition: to get rid of a thought, doubt, or unwanted influence completely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底去掉某种念头、疑虑或不良影响
senses.example: She tried to expel the memory from her mind.
senses.exampleCN: 她试着把那段记忆从脑中祛除。
senses.why: A mind is treated as a container, and an unwelcome thought as an object to be pushed out of it.
senses.whyCN: 头脑被当作容器，不受欢迎的念头则成了要被推出去的物件。

intro.en: Expel comes from Latin expellere, to drive out, from ex-, out, and pellere, to drive.
intro.cn: expel 来自拉丁语 expellere（赶出去），由 ex-（向外）与 pellere（推、赶）合成。

items.en: Pellere means to drive or push, as a herdsman drives cattle.
items.cn: pellere 意为推、赶，就像牧人赶牛。

items.en: Expellere joins ex-, out, with pellere: to drive a person or thing out.
items.cn: expellere 把 ex-（向外）与 pellere 结合，义为把人或物赶出去。

items.en: The participle expulsus feeds the noun expulsio, a driving out.
items.cn: 分词 expulsus 派生名词 expulsio，义为「逐出」。

items.en: Expeller carries the verb into French with the same force.
items.cn: expeller 把这个动词带入法语，力度不变。

items.en: Expellen appears in English for driving a person out of a place.
items.cn: 中古英语 expellen 指把人从一个地方赶出去。

items.en: Later usage adds gas, cartridges, players, and unwanted thoughts.
items.cn: 后来的用法又加上气体、弹壳、球员以及不受欢迎的念头。

note.en: Expel belongs to the Latin driving family, so impel, propel, and repel are its closest relatives, while eject and deport cover single senses.
note.cn: expel 属于拉丁语「推、赶」词族，impel、propel、repel 是它最近的亲戚，而 eject 与 deport 各只覆盖其中一个义项。

entries.definition: the act of forcing someone out of a place or group
entries.definitionCN: 把人逐出某地或某团体的行为

entries.definition: a person who has been expelled
to urge or force someone to act
entries.definitionCN: 推动、迫使某人行动（同根，前缀 in- 向内）

entries.definition: to force something out, especially from a machine
entries.definitionCN: 把某物弹出或排出，尤指从机器中

entries.definition: to send a foreigner out of a country by law
entries.definitionCN: 依法把外国人遣送出境

entries.definition: to remove someone from a job or a class
entries.definitionCN: 把某人免职或从班里除名

normalIntro.en: Expel is the Latin verb of driving, and every sense keeps a hand pushing something outward.
normalIntro.cn: expel 是拉丁语中表示「推、赶」的动词，每个义项里都有一只手把东西往外推。

normal.en: Ex- means out and pellere means to drive, so expel is to drive someone out.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex- 表示「向外」，pellere 表示「推、赶」，所以 expel 就是把人往外赶。

normal.en: Schools expel students, and countries expel diplomats.
normal.cn: 学校开除学生，国家驱逐外交官。

normal.en: The frame be expelled from is the usual passive pattern.
normal.cn: 被动句式「be expelled from」是最常见的框架。

normal.en: The noun is expulsion, not the invented form expelment.
normal.cn: 名词是 expulsion，而不是生造的 expelment。

normal.en: Compare impel: in- points inward, so impel is to drive someone on from within.
normal.cn: 对比 impel：前缀 in- 指向内，所以 impel 是从内部推动某人。

abstract.en: Picture a hand flat on a back, steering a boy through a gate that shuts behind him.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在背上，把男孩推过校门，门在身后关上。

abstract.en: Picture a passport stamped and a car already waiting at the border.
abstract.cn: 想象护照被盖上章，一辆车已经在边境等着。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle spout and a puff of steam shooting out.
abstract.cn: 想象壶嘴喷出一股蒸汽。

examples.en: He was expelled from the club for breaking the rules.
examples.cn: 他因违反规定被俱乐部开除。

examples.en: The pump expels water through a narrow pipe.
examples.cn: 水泵通过细管把水排出。

examples.en: The government expelled two diplomats last month.
examples.cn: 政府上月驱逐了两名外交官。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一克斯佩尔」——听上去像被人一把推出门外，这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语「expellere」＝「ex-」（向外）+「pellere」（推、赶），过去分词「expulsus」给出名词「expulsio」。同根词有「impel」（向内推，故为促使）、「propel」（向前推，故为推进）、「repel」（推回去，故为击退）。

sensesIntro.en: Expel is one outward push, applied first to members and foreigners, then to matter, players, and finally to thoughts.
sensesIntro.cn: expel 就是一次向外的推，先落在成员与外国人身上，再落到物质、球员，最后落到念头身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand pushing a body through a doorway.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一个身体推过门口。

branches.en: The school sense keeps the institutional door.
branches.cn: 学校义项保留的是制度之门。

branches.en: The national sense puts the door at a border.
branches.cn: 国家义项把这道门安在国界上。

branches.en: Matter instead of people is pushed out.
branches.cn: 被推出去的对象由人换成了物质。

branches.en: Hands and rules both push a body off a floor.
branches.cn: 双手与规则都在把一个身体推离场地。

branches.en: The container becomes a mind, and the pushed object a thought.
branches.cn: 容器变成头脑，被推出去的物件变成念头。

intro.en: Expel is a Latin verb of driving, with the family impel, propel, repel and the noun expulsion built on the same stem.
intro.cn: expel 是拉丁语中表示「推、赶」的动词，同族有 impel、propel、repel，名词 expulsion 建于同一词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin pellere means to drive, and expellere means to drive out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pellere 意为推、赶，expellere 意为赶出去。

items.example: The prefix ex- marks the outward direction of expel.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 标出 expel 向外的方向。

items.example: Pellere supplies the pushing force in expel.
items.exampleCN: pellere 为 expel 提供推的力量。

items.example: Expellere is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: expellere 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: Expulsus gives the stem used in expulsion.
items.exampleCN: expulsus 提供 expulsion 所用的词干。

items.meaningCN: 动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -sion forms expulsion from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -sion 在拉丁词干上构成 expulsion。

items.example: Expulsion names the act, not the person.
items.exampleCN: expulsion 指行为本身，不指人。

items.meaning: a person who receives an action
items.example: The suffix -ee forms expellee.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ee 构成 expellee。

items.example: Expellee is the person at the receiving end.
items.exampleCN: expellee 是承受这一动作的那个人。

items.example: Impel turns the same root inward.
items.exampleCN: impel 把同一词根转向内部。

items.example: Propel points the push forward.
items.exampleCN: propel 把推力指向前方。

definition_en: the amount of money spent; the act of spending money; the use of time or energy
core_image: 一笔钱被称量后付出去
scene: 政府计划削减明年的公共开支。The government plans to cut public expenditure next year.
sceneCN: 这里 expenditure 是「支出、经费」（第 1 个义项）；句意：政府计划削减明年的公共开支。

senses.title: Money spent
senses.definition: the amount of money that is spent
senses.definitionCN: 花出去的钱的总额
senses.example: Public expenditure rose sharply last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年公共开支大幅上升。
senses.why: The noun names money paid out.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指付出去的钱。

senses.title: Budget item
senses.definition: a particular sum of money used for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某一用途拨出的一笔钱
senses.example: The school increased its expenditure on books.
senses.exampleCN: 学校增加了购书经费。
senses.why: Money paid out is organized into budget items.
senses.whyCN: 支出的钱被归入预算项目。

senses.title: Use of energy
senses.definition: the use of time, energy, or effort
senses.definitionCN: 时间、精力或努力的使用
senses.example: The project required a huge expenditure of energy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目需要消耗巨大的精力。
senses.why: Spending extends from money to effort.
senses.whyCN: 「花费」从金钱扩展到精力。

intro.en: Expenditure comes from Latin expendere, to weigh out and pay.
intro.cn: expenditure 源自拉丁语 expendere，意为「称量后付出」。

items.en: Expendere means to weigh out and pay.
items.cn: expendere 意为称量后支付。

items.en: It joins ex- (out) with pendere (to weigh).
items.cn: 它由 ex-（向外）与 pendere（称量）构成。

items.en: Expenditura names money paid out.
items.cn: expenditura 指付出去的钱。

items.en: Expenditure is used in accounts.
items.cn: expenditure 出现在账目用语中。

items.en: Expenditure covers money and energy used.
items.cn: expenditure 涵盖花掉的钱与消耗的精力。

items.en: Public expenditure is a common phrase.
items.cn: public expenditure 成为常用搭配。

note.en: Expenditure is money paid out; an expedition is a journey.
note.cn: expenditure 是支出，expedition 则是远征。

entries.definition: able to be used up or sacrificed
an organized journey
the state of being uncovered
money that is spent
the amount paid for something
money spent on a project

normalIntro.en: Expenditure is the money or energy you pay out.
normalIntro.cn: expenditure 就是你付出去的钱或精力。

normal.en: The city reduced expenditure on new roads.
normal.cn: 市里削减了新修道路的开支。

normal.en: Capital expenditure rose with the new factory.
normal.cn: 随着新工厂建设，资本支出上升。

normal.en: They kept a record of every expenditure.
normal.cn: 他们记录每一笔支出。

normal.en: The rescue needed a great expenditure of effort.
normal.cn: 那次救援耗费了巨大的努力。

normal.en: Health expenditure takes a large share of the budget.
normal.cn: 医疗开支占预算的很大一部分。

abstract.en: Picture coins weighed on a small scale.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币在小秤上被称量。

abstract.en: Imagine a ledger with columns of payments.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记满付款栏目的账簿。

abstract.en: Think of energy pouring out like water.
abstract.cn: 想象精力像水一样流出去。

examples.en: The report tracks government expenditure each year.
examples.cn: 这份报告追踪每年的政府开支。

examples.en: They argued about the expenditure on the new bridge.
examples.cn: 他们为修建新桥的开支争论不休。

examples.en: The task demanded a large expenditure of time.
examples.cn: 这项任务需要投入大量时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「expenditure」里有 expend（花费）：把钱包里的钱向外称出去，就是「支出」。

root: 拉丁语 expendere（称量后支付）由 ex-（向外）与 pendere（称量）构成，核心义「把钱称出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Expenditure means money spent, a budget item, or the use of time and energy.
sensesIntro.cn: expenditure 意为花掉的钱、一笔经费，或时间与精力的消耗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: money weighed and paid out.
core.cn: 核心意象：把钱包称量后付出去。

branches.en: The base sense is money paid out.
branches.cn: 基础义是付出的钱。

branches.en: Payments are grouped into budget lines.
branches.cn: 付款被归入预算项目。

branches.en: Paying out extends to effort and time.
branches.cn: 「付出」扩展到精力与时间。

branches.en: Total spending and single items pair together.
branches.cn: 总支出与单项经费相互对应。

branches.en: Money and energy are both resources spent.
branches.cn: 金钱与精力都是被消耗的资源。

intro.cn: expenditure 在 expend 后加后缀 -ure。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 expendere 与 expenditura 提供核心词形。

items.example: Ex- marks paying out.

items.example: Pendere gives the image of weighing money.

items.example: Expendere is the source of expend.

items.example: Expenditura leads to English expenditure.

items.example: -Ure forms nouns of action.

definition_en: the money needed or spent for something; something that costs money; the loss or sacrifice involved
core_image: 为得到某样东西而付出的钱
scene: 他把差旅费用记在了公司账上。He put the travel expenses on the company account.
sceneCN: 这里 expense 是「费用、开支」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他把差旅费用记在了公司账上。

senses.title: Cost of something
senses.definition: the money needed or spent for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事物所需或所花的钱
senses.example: The expense of the trip was too high.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟旅行的费用太高了。
senses.why: The base sense is money laid out.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是付出去的钱。

senses.title: Money for work
senses.definition: money spent for a particular purpose, often repaid by an employer
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途支出、常由雇主报销的钱
senses.example: She kept every receipt to claim her expenses.
senses.exampleCN: 她保留每张收据以便报销。
senses.why: The cost is tied to a job or purpose.
senses.whyCN: 费用与工作或特定用途绑定。

senses.title: Price paid
senses.definition: the loss or sacrifice involved in gaining something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而付出的损失或牺牲
senses.example: He won the race at the expense of his health.
senses.exampleCN: 他以健康为代价赢得了比赛。
senses.why: Money cost becomes any kind of cost.
senses.whyCN: 金钱成本扩展为任何代价。

intro.cn: expense 源自拉丁语 expensa，意为「付出去的钱」。

items.en: Expensa is money paid out.

items.en: Expendere means to weigh out and spend.

items.en: Espense keeps the sense of cost.

items.en: Expense enters as a business term.

definition_en: knowledge or skill gained by doing something; an event that you go through; to feel or undergo something
core_image: 亲自走过一段路后留在心里的东西
scene: 她在这个行业有十年的工作经验。She has ten years of experience in the industry.
sceneCN: 这里 experience 是「经验」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在这个行业有十年的工作经验。

senses.title: Knowledge from doing
senses.definition: knowledge or skill gained by doing something
senses.definitionCN: 通过做事获得的知识或技能

senses.title: Event you live through

senses.why: The knowledge comes from a particular event.

senses.title: To undergo

senses.why: The noun turns into the act of living through.

intro.cn: experience 源自拉丁语 experientia，意为「通过尝试得到的知识」。

contact with something new

normalIntro.cn: experience 是你亲身经历后留下的收获。

normal.en: The job gave him useful experience.
normal.cn: 这份工作给了他有用的经验。

normal.cn: 在国外生活是一段丰富的经历。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「experience」可拆成 ex（出）+ peri（尝试）+ ence：一次次尝试走出来的东西，就是「经验」。

root: 拉丁语 experiri（尝试、试验）的名词 experientia 进入英语，核心义「亲身试过之后得到的知识」。

sensesIntro.en: Experience means skill from practice, an event you live through, or to undergo something.
sensesIntro.cn: experience 意为实践得来的经验、亲身经历的事件，或经历某事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trace left by walking a road yourself.
core.cn: 核心意象：亲自走过一条路后留下的痕迹。

branches.en: The base sense is knowledge from practice.
branches.cn: 基础义是实践得来的知识。

branches.en: Knowledge is tied to one lived event.
branches.cn: 知识绑定于某次亲历事件。

branches.en: The noun becomes the act of undergoing.
branches.cn: 名词转化为经历的动作。

branches.en: Skill and event both come from living through.
branches.cn: 技能与事件都来自亲身经历。

branches.en: An event and feeling it are closely linked.
branches.cn: 事件与感受它的动作紧密相连。

intro.en: Experience comes from Latin experiri with the noun suffix -ence.
intro.cn: experience 来自拉丁语 experiri，并带名词后缀 -ence。

latinIntro.en: Latin experiri and experientia supply the core forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 experiri 与 experientia 提供核心词形。

items.example: Ex- marks trying something out.
items.exampleCN: ex- 表示把某事试出来。

items.example: Periri gives the sense of testing.
items.exampleCN: periri 提供「试验」的含义。

items.example: Experiri is the source of experience.
items.exampleCN: experiri 是 experience 的来源。

items.example: Experientia gives English experience.
items.exampleCN: experientia 演变为英语 experience。

items.example: -Ence forms abstract nouns.
items.exampleCN: -ence 构成抽象名词。

items.example: Experience names what practice gives.
items.exampleCN: experience 指实践带来的东西。

items.example: -Ed forms experienced.
items.exampleCN: -ed 构成 experienced。

items.example: Experienced describes a skilled person.
items.exampleCN: experienced 形容有技能的人。

items.example: -Ial forms experiential.
items.exampleCN: -ial 构成 experiential。

items.example: Experiential learning uses direct practice.
items.exampleCN: 体验式学习依靠直接实践。

definition_en: a scientific test to learn something; a trial of a new idea; to try something new
core_image: 在受控条件下反复试一件事，看结果如何
scene: 学生们在实验室里重复了这个实验。The students repeated the experiment in the lab.
sceneCN: 这里 experiment 是「实验」（第 1 个义项）；句意：学生们在实验室里重复了这个实验。

senses.title: Scientific test
senses.definition: a scientific test done to learn something
senses.definitionCN: 为了解某事而进行的科学测试
senses.example: The experiment proved the theory wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验证明该理论是错的。
senses.why: The core sense is a controlled test.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是受控的测试。

senses.title: Trial of an idea
senses.definition: a trial of a new idea or method
senses.definitionCN: 对新想法或新方法的试行
senses.example: The school ran an experiment in outdoor lessons.
senses.exampleCN: 学校试行了一种户外课堂。
senses.why: Science extends to social and personal trials.
senses.whyCN: 科学实验扩展到社会与个人层面的尝试。

senses.title: To try new things
senses.definition: to try something new or different
senses.definitionCN: 尝试新事物或不同的做法
senses.example: He experimented with different colors.
senses.exampleCN: 他尝试了不同的颜色。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of trying.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为尝试的动作。

intro.en: Experiment comes from Latin experimentum, a trial or proof.
intro.cn: experiment 源自拉丁语 experimentum，意为「试验、证明」。

items.en: Experimentum names a trial or proof.
items.cn: experimentum 指试验或证明。

items.en: It comes from experiri, to try.
items.cn: 它来自 experiri，意为尝试。

items.en: Experiment keeps the sense of testing.
items.cn: experiment 保留测试的含义。

items.en: Experiment enters the language of science.
items.cn: experiment 进入科学语言。

items.en: Experiment adds the sense of a new trial.
items.cn: experiment 增加了「新尝试」之义。

items.en: Experiment with becomes a common verb phrase.
items.cn: experiment with 成为常见的动词搭配。

note.en: An experiment is a test; experience is knowledge from living.
note.cn: experiment 是测试，experience 则是亲身经历得来的知识。

entries.definition: knowledge gained by doing
someone with special skill
useful though possibly improper
a procedure to check something
a period of testing something
research into a subject

normalIntro.en: An experiment is a test you run to find out.
normalIntro.cn: experiment 是为了弄清问题而做的测试。

normal.en: The class did a simple experiment with water.
normal.cn: 全班用水做了一个简单实验。

normal.en: The company ran an experiment in shorter hours.
normal.cn: 公司试行了缩短工时的做法。

normal.en: She experimented with a new recipe.
normal.cn: 她尝试了一种新食谱。

normal.en: The experiment failed and they tried again.
normal.cn: 实验失败后他们又试了一次。

normal.en: A good experiment needs a clear control.
normal.cn: 好的实验需要清晰的对照。

abstract.en: Picture two glass tubes side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象并排放着的两根玻璃管。

abstract.en: Imagine changing one thing and watching the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象只改变一件事并观察其余变化。

abstract.en: Think of a notebook full of trial results.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记满试验结果的笔记。

examples.en: The experiment showed that plants need light.
examples.cn: 实验表明植物需要光。

examples.en: They experimented with solar power on the roof.
examples.cn: 他们在屋顶上试验太阳能。

examples.en: The new teaching method is still an experiment.
examples.cn: 这种新教学法仍是一种试验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「experiment」里有 peri（尝试）：反复试、反复测，就是「实验」。

root: 拉丁语 experimentum（试验、证明）来自 experiri（尝试），核心义「通过尝试求得证明」。

sensesIntro.en: Experiment means a scientific test, a trial of a new idea, or to try something new.
sensesIntro.cn: experiment 意为科学实验、对新想法的试行，或尝试新事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a controlled trial with a clear result.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次有明确结果的受控试验。

branches.en: The base sense is a scientific test.
branches.cn: 基础义是科学实验。

branches.en: Testing extends to social trials.
branches.cn: 测试扩展到社会层面的试行。

branches.en: The noun becomes the act of trying.
branches.cn: 名词转化为尝试的动作。

branches.en: Both are structured ways of finding out.
branches.cn: 两者都是有结构的探知方式。

branches.en: A trial and trying it out belong together.
branches.cn: 试行与动手尝试相互关联。

intro.en: Experiment builds on experiri with the noun ending -ment.
intro.cn: experiment 在 experiri 基础上加名词词尾 -ment。

latinIntro.en: Latin experimentum and experiri supply the core forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 experimentum 与 experiri 提供核心词形。

items.example: Ex- marks trying something out.
items.exampleCN: ex- 表示把某事试出来。

items.example: Periri gives the sense of testing.
items.exampleCN: periri 提供「试验」的含义。

items.example: Experiri is the source verb.
items.exampleCN: experiri 是来源动词。

items.example: Experimentum gives English experiment.
items.exampleCN: experimentum 演变为英语 experiment。

items.example: -Ment forms nouns from verbs.
items.exampleCN: -ment 把动词变成名词。

items.example: Experiment names the test.
items.exampleCN: experiment 指这种测试。

items.example: -Al forms experimental.
items.exampleCN: -al 构成 experimental。

items.example: Experimental describes test work.
items.exampleCN: experimental 描述实验性质的工作。

definition_zh: 专业知识；专门技能；专长
definition_en: a high level of knowledge or skill in a particular field, gained by training and long practice
core_image: 一双手在看不见的地方也能摸准零件的位置
scene: 修表匠的手指在细小齿轮间移动，那是多年积累的专长。The watchmaker moved among the tiny gears with the expertise of forty years.
sceneCN: 这里 expertise 是「专业知识与技能」（第 1 个义项：在某一领域达到很高水平的知识与本领）；句意：修表匠带着四十年练就的专长，在细小齿轮间操作。

pos.zh: 专业知识；专门技能；专长

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「专家」；expertise 由它加名词词尾构成
由 expert 加 -ness 构成，义为「老练；专长」
由 expert 加 -ly 构成，义为「熟练地」
由 expert 加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不熟练的」

senses.title: Expert knowledge and skill in a field
senses.definition: a high level of knowledge or skill in a particular subject, gained by training and practice
senses.definitionCN: 在某一学科或领域达到很高水平的知识与本领，来自训练与长期实践
senses.example: The job calls for expertise in data analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作需要数据分析方面的专长。
senses.why: Latin experiri means to try or test, so expertise is what repeated testing leaves behind in a person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 experiri 意为尝试、检验，所以专长就是反复检验之后留在一个人身上的东西。

senses.title: The specialist knowledge a profession requires
senses.definition: the body of specialist knowledge that a trade or profession depends on
senses.definitionCN: 某个行业或职业所依赖的一整套专门知识
senses.example: Medical expertise cannot be picked up from a handbook.
senses.exampleCN: 医学的专业知识无法从手册里随手学来。
senses.why: When a whole trade shares tested knowledge, the word names that knowledge rather than the skill of one person.
senses.whyCN: 当整个行业共享这套经过检验的知识时，这个词指的就是知识本身，而不是某个人的本领。

senses.title: Practical skill in a craft
senses.definition: the hands-on skill that comes from long practice at a craft
senses.definitionCN: 长期从事一门手艺而养成的动手本领
senses.example: Her expertise with a chisel showed in every joint.
senses.exampleCN: 她使凿子的功夫在每一处榫接上都看得出来。
senses.why: What gets tested is not only a statement but a movement of the hand.
senses.whyCN: 被反复检验的不只是一句判断，还有手上的一个动作。

senses.title: The authority that comes from being an expert
senses.definition: the standing or confidence that specialist knowledge gives a person
senses.definitionCN: 专门知识赋予一个人的地位与可信度
senses.example: The committee deferred to his expertise on the region.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在这个地区的问题上听从他的专业判断。
senses.why: Knowledge that has been tested earns trust, and trust is a kind of social weight.
senses.whyCN: 经得起检验的知识会赢得信任，而信任是一种社会分量。

senses.title: An expert appraisal or opinion
senses.definition: a judgement or report given by a specialist, especially in formal or legal settings
senses.definitionCN: 由专家给出的判断或报告，尤见于正式或法律场合
senses.example: The court ordered an expertise on the damaged wall.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭下令对受损的墙体作一次鉴定。
senses.why: French expertise names the report itself, and English keeps this countable, formal sense at the edges.
senses.whyCN: 法语 expertise 本就指那份鉴定报告，英语在边缘地带保留了这一可数的正式义项。

intro.en: Expertise is a French noun built on expert, which comes from Latin expertus, having tried, from experiri, to test.
intro.cn: expertise 是建筑在 expert 之上的法语名词，而 expert 来自拉丁语 expertus（试过的），源自动词 experiri（检验）。

items.en: Experiri means to try or test, and its participle expertus means having tried, hence experienced.
items.cn: experiri 意为尝试、检验，其分词 expertus 意为「试过的」，因此指有经验的。

items.en: The same idea of trial underlies experimentum, a test, and periculum, a danger.
items.cn: 同样的「试」的观念也支撑着 experimentum（试验）与 periculum（危险）。

items.en: Old French expertise names a skilled appraisal or the report that records it.
items.cn: 古法语 expertise 指内行的估价，或记录该估价的报告。

items.en: Modern French keeps expertise as the ordinary word for an expert assessment.
items.cn: 现代法语仍用 expertise 表示专家评估。

items.en: English borrows the word in the nineteenth century for expert skill or a specialist report.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入这个词，用来指专家的本领或专家报告。

items.en: The report sense narrows, and the word now chiefly means specialist knowledge and skill.
items.cn: 报告这一义项收窄，如今这个词主要指专门的知识与技能。

note.en: Expertise sits inside the expert family, and it is close in meaning to plain skill words that carry no claim of specialist standing.
note.cn: expertise 位于 expert 词族之中，意思上又靠近那些不强调专家身份的普通「技能」词。

entries.definition: a person with special knowledge of a subject
entries.definitionCN: 对某一学科有专门知识的人

entries.definition: the quality of being expert
in a skilful manner
the ability to do something well, gained by practice
entries.definitionCN: 通过练习获得的、做好某事的能力

entries.definition: a high degree of competence in an activity
entries.definitionCN: 在某一活动中达到的高水平

entries.definition: practical knowledge of how to do something
entries.definitionCN: 关于如何做某事的实用知识

normalIntro.en: Expertise is the French noun of expert, and the whole family grows from the Latin verb for testing.
normalIntro.cn: expertise 是 expert 的法语名词形式，整个词族都长在拉丁语那个表示「检验」的动词上。

normal.en: Expert plus the French noun ending -ise gives expertise.
normal.cn: expert 加上法语名词词尾 -ise，构成 expertise。

normal.en: Technical expertise is the most common collocation in modern use.
normal.cn: 「technical expertise」是现代用法里最常见的搭配。

normal.en: An area of expertise is the field where someone is trusted.
normal.cn: 「an area of expertise」指某人被信赖的那个领域。

normal.en: To draw on the expertise of a team is to use what it knows.
normal.cn: 「draw on the expertise of a team」意思是借助团队掌握的知识。

normal.en: Compare experience: the same Latin root, but one is lived time and the other is tested skill.
normal.cn: 对比 experience：同一个拉丁词根，一个指亲身经历的时间，一个指经过检验的本领。

abstract.en: Picture a watchmaker closing both eyes and still finding the right screw.
abstract.cn: 想象修表匠闭上双眼，仍然摸得到对的那颗螺丝。

abstract.en: Picture a hospital ward where every nurse knows the same emergency steps by heart.
abstract.cn: 想象一间病房里，每位护士都把同一套急救步骤背得烂熟。

abstract.en: Picture a carpenter running a plane along a board without stopping to measure.
abstract.cn: 想象木匠推着刨子一路走完木板，中途不用停下来量。

examples.en: The project needs technical expertise rather than enthusiasm.
examples.cn: 这个项目需要技术专长，而不是热情。

examples.en: She built her expertise over twenty years of fieldwork.
examples.cn: 她用二十年的野外工作积累起自己的专长。

examples.en: We asked for expertise from outside the department.
examples.cn: 我们向部门之外寻求专业意见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱克斯破泰兹」——听上去像老师傅一摸就知道，靠的是多年积累，这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 法语「expertise」（专家鉴定）←「expert」（内行的）← 拉丁语「expertus」（试过的、有经验的），源自动词「experiri」（尝试、检验）。同根词有「experience」（经验）与「experiment」（实验）。

sensesIntro.en: Expertise begins as tested knowledge in one person, spreads to the knowledge a trade owns, then to the authority and the formal report that knowledge produces.
sensesIntro.cn: expertise 先是某个人身上经过检验的知识，再扩展为一个行业共有的知识，最后延伸到这种知识带来的权威与正式鉴定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands that find the right part without looking.
core.cn: 核心意象：不用看也能摸准零件的双手。

branches.en: Tested knowledge in one person is the central modern sense.
branches.cn: 某个人身上经过检验的知识，是核心的现代义项。

branches.en: A whole profession owns a body of such knowledge.
branches.cn: 整个行业拥有一整套这样的知识。

branches.en: The testing is done by the hand as much as by the head.
branches.cn: 接受检验的，手上和脑里一样多。

branches.en: Knowledge that survives testing becomes authority, and authority can be delivered as a report.
branches.cn: 经得起检验的知识变成权威，而权威可以以一份报告的形式交付。

branches.en: The shared knowledge of a trade and the formal appraisal both speak with the weight of a profession.
branches.cn: 行业共有的知识与正式鉴定，都带着一个职业的分量说话。

intro.en: Expertise is a French noun on expert, and the English family adds expertness, expertly, and inexpert around it.
intro.cn: expertise 是建筑在 expert 上的法语名词，英语在它周围又添了 expertness、expertly 与 inexpert。

latinIntro.en: Latin experiri means to try or test, and expertus means having tried.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 experiri 意为尝试、检验，expertus 意为试过的。

items.example: Experiri is the verb that starts the whole family.
items.exampleCN: experiri 是整个词族起步的那个动词。

items.example: Expertus is the participle behind expert.
items.exampleCN: expertus 是 expert 背后的那个分词。

items.example: Expert names the person who has done the testing.
items.exampleCN: expert 指完成过检验的那个人。

items.example: The adjective expert describes a skilled hand.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 expert 描述一双熟练的手。

items.meaningCN: 状态、性质或职业的名词词尾
items.example: The French suffix -ise turns expert into expertise.
items.exampleCN: 法语词尾 -ise 把 expert 变成 expertise。

items.example: Expertise keeps the abstract sense of the French noun.
items.exampleCN: expertise 保留了法语名词的抽象含义。

items.meaningCN: 状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms expertness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 expertness。

items.example: Expertness is the plainer native rival of expertise.
items.exampleCN: expertness 是 expertise 更朴素的本地同义词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms expertly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 expertly。

items.example: Expertly describes how the work is done.
items.exampleCN: expertly 描述这件活是怎么做的。
